plays.title: They give the courtesy memory at the gate
plays.why: It is presented as a formality, the clerk is pitiable, and refusing looks like trouble on the first day.
plays.tells: Players ask “What happens to it?” or start choosing something small.
plays.readAloud: The clerk touches a tuning fork to a vial of grey glass and holds it near your temple. It feels like forgetting a word you were about to say, and then not minding. He writes your name in the book without looking up. “Welcome to Hallowmere. You won't miss it.”
plays.response: Each player chooses the memory and writes one line in the Memory Ledger; you never choose it. Log it as a Tithe, not a Toll: it sits in a labelled jar in the Tithe-Ledger Room and its owner can redeem it by opening the jar. Clerk Oswin Tell is a Blank; asked why he works here, he says “Someone must,” and looks frightened that he cannot say who. If anyone offers gold he stares at the coin as if it were a pebble: the courtesy memory is a registration, not a fee, and the Hallowmere gate takes no gold for it.
plays.rules: No check. Record as a Tithe (redeemable), not a Toll. A Reckoner's draw takes about a minute and needs consent.
plays.consequence: The party is in the Tithe-system. Any Hushman can look up their names and what they gave.
plays.later: S5: each courtesy jar sits on the vault's newest shelf, near the character's older earliest-memory jar. S7 and S9: Hushmen at the line and the north gate know their names on sight.
plays.fallback: If a player can't pick, offer a mote: last Ossday's supper, a stranger's coat, the second verse of a song.
plays.keywords: gate, courtesy memory, register, registration, tithe, clerk, give memory, entry, gold, pay, oswin

plays.title: They refuse the courtesy memory
plays.why: Players who spent three sessions learning what the Tithe costs will balk at feeding it.
plays.tells: A flat “No,” or a player asks what happens if they don't.
plays.readAloud: The clerk's pen stops. He looks past you, at the two grey-gloved men by the arch, and says in a small voice, “Sergeant? These ones won't.”
plays.response: Refusing needs Influence (Persuasion) DC 15 on Sergeant Mabry Cole, or a bribe: Cole takes 10 gp a head, Tithes a mote of his own to fill the line, and pockets the gold. If that fails, Cole calls his men (Gate Hushmen). The party can run into the lamp-lit lanes (DC 13 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) each) or talk their way out (DC 15 Charisma (Deception): 'the Chancellor promised us exemption'). Anyone who fails spends a day and a night in a cell in Vaer's Belfry, and Captain Rook hears of it by evening and visits the cell herself.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 (Cole's Intelligence is 14). Athletics or Acrobatics DC 13 to flee; Deception DC 15. Quill's modifiers: add +2 to these DCs if quill is Suspicious, Tithe-case or Dead (the Gate Clerk has their names; if Dead, Cole names them murderers); subtract 2 if quill is Bribed (Quill's letter vouches for them). Add +2 more if the party carried the Tongue to Hallowmere early in S3. A night in the Belfry is a night in a Court city (Tithe Clock +1).
plays.consequence: The party stays outside the Tithe-system, and the gate remembers their faces as refusers.
plays.later: S6: a jailed character meets Rook early; she opens the commission in the cell. S9: Cole is on the north gate on the day they leave and remembers refusers (+2 to any bluff there).
plays.fallback: If it bogs down, the Assembly's carriage arrives for 'the Chancellor's guests' and Cole steps back, furious.
plays.keywords: refuse, no, won't give, bribe guard, run, flee, gate, hushmen, deception, belfry, jail, cell, cole, sergeant

plays.title: A Stormborn character shows their papers
plays.why: Under the Landing Charter, Faerûnians need a writ of passage beyond the Mere road, and the Hallowmere gate checks.
plays.tells: A Sword Coast character produces papers, or asks whether foreigners are allowed in.
plays.readAloud: Sergeant Cole holds the grey-sealed letter to the lamp and reads the signature twice. Then he hands it back very carefully, as if it might bruise. “Guests of the Assembly. Loudfolk too, it seems.”
plays.response: Read the writ. The Chancellor's invitation (writ Invited) counts for everyone it names, Stormborn included. A true writ (bought from Quill) passes without a question. A forged writ gets past the Blank clerk but not Cole, who checks the grey wax (DC 17 Intelligence (Investigation)); a failed forgery is arrest for 'landing past the Charter' unless they talk or run as above. With no writ at all, a Faerûnian is turned back to the Mere road; a Corvane Venture cloth wagon gets them in by night (DC 16 Dexterity (Stealth)). Inland, nobody speaks Common: Faerûnians without Hesk need a companion to translate, or Comprehend Languages to understand what is said; a Hesk speaker still has to speak for them.
plays.rules: Investigation DC 17 (Cole vs a forgery). Stealth DC 16 to ride in under cloth. Add Quill's modifier from s04-refuse-courtesy-memory. Comprehend Languages lets you understand Hesk but not reply in it; Tongues is a level-5 spell.
plays.consequence: Stormborn characters are inside Hallowmere, lawfully or not. Hushmen stare at dragonborn, tieflings and gnomes, and whisper that aasimar are bell-touched.
plays.later: S9: a forged-writ character is stopped at the north gate unless they leave under Rook's escort or a smuggling route. Act IV: if Thrane rings, the Charter collapses and writs stop mattering.
plays.fallback: If a player feels locked out, a palace clerk arrives with a fresh writ 'for the Chancellor's guests', which also shows how closely Maudrin watches them.
plays.keywords: writ, passage, papers, faerunian, stormborn, loudfolk, foreigner, forged, seal, grey wax, charter, hesk, language, tongues, translate

plays.title: They bring Sister Aurelie into the city
plays.why: The Court has refused Aurelie's writ four times; a party with the Chancellor's invitation looks like her chance.
plays.tells: The party met Aurelie at the Dawn Mission (s01-dawn-mission), or a cleric or paladin of Lathander asks about her.
plays.readAloud: Sister Aurelie lowers her hood at the edge of the marsh road and looks up at the grey disc of the sun. “When the sun comes back,” she says, “I'd like to be standing somewhere it can see me.”
plays.response: The invitation does not name her. Passing her off as the party's scribe is Influence (Deception) DC 15 against Cole; hiding her in a cart is DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth) for her, with advantage if someone Helps. Inside, she cannot stay quiet: within two days she wants to sing a dawn-hymn on the Terraces of Grief. If caught, play s04-aurelie-caught.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 (Cole). Stealth DC 15; Help gives advantage. Aurelie uses Priest stats (Healing Word, Lesser Restoration, Dispel Magic: she is an NPC, so her 3rd-level spells are not available to the party).
plays.consequence: Aurelie is in Hallowmere: a healer, an ally, and a liability.
plays.later: S9: if Vaer rings while she is in the city, she goes to the terraces to sing (s09-aurelie-on-the-terraces). S22: a free Aurelie is the core of the Stormborn ally.
plays.fallback: If smuggling her stalls, she gives the party a letter for 'the Dawn Mission's first friend in Hallowmere' and goes back to Pellmoor to wait.
plays.keywords: aurelie, dawnmantle, lathander, dawn mission, morninglord, smuggle, sneak in, cart, cleric, priest, disguise

plays.title: They stayed to defend Pellmoor
plays.why: A party that kept the Tongue in Pellmoor (S3) opens Act II under siege instead of at the gate.
plays.tells: The Tongue is still in Pellmoor and Quill's notice is on the chapel door.
plays.readAloud: The notice is nailed to the chapel door in Quill's neat hand: 'By the Office of Tithes. Surrender all unlicensed bell-work by Hushday dusk. Thereafter the Old Shore will be searched house by house.'
plays.response: Run it short: Quill gives three days. The villagers want a shelter (the ledger-house) and an escape route (Brannagh Wick's pilots can take the Old Shore across the Mere in two nights). The households who owe the party (s01-fill-the-quota) shelter villagers without being asked. The party negotiates, resists one patrol (Siege Patrol), or leads the evacuation. Whatever happens, the patrol's Sergeant carries orders in grey wax: 'Ossa relic to the Tithe-Ledger Room, Hallowmere, by Vaerday.' The siege takes three days and the road to the capital three more; the Assembly is ten days after the letter, so they arrive with a day to spare. The marsh road out is cordoned (DC 16 Dexterity (Stealth) as a group). The outcome is s04-evacuate-old-shore or s04-siege-holds.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 16 past the cordon; Pass without Trace gives +10. Influence DC 15 on Quill (Indifferent, Hostile if the party is a Tithe-case).
plays.consequence: Pellmoor is under siege. The party chooses how it ends.
plays.later: S9: the party can come back to Pellmoor instead of going north. S22: defended ferry-folk keep Court ships on the Mere for a day (no pilot, no departure).
plays.fallback: If the siege drags, Quill accepts a parley: one memory 'for the quota' from a volunteer, and he withdraws for a week.
plays.keywords: siege, defend pellmoor, quill, deadline, evacuate, cordon, marsh road, patrol, orders, old shore, stay

plays.title: They refuse the invitation or never go to the Assembly
plays.why: Some tables smell a trap and stay away from the Chancellor entirely.
plays.tells: “We're not going to her party.” Or they head straight for the Bone Archive or the Dawn Order.
plays.readAloud: A broad woman in a dawn-coloured cloak gone grey sits down across from you without asking and sets a Dawn Order seal on the table. “You turned down the Chancellor. Good. Then you might be the only people in this city who'll listen to me.”
plays.response: Bring the investigation to them. Captain Dessa Rook finds them at their lodgings and opens her commission early (S6, Scene 1); or Wren Caddock, sewing on a bench outside the Bone Archive, asks too many friendly questions and mentions that Lysse Carrow 'needs someone brave'. Maudrin is not offended: she sends a single grey rose to their lodgings with no note, and two Hushmen follow them for the rest of the Act.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 15 to shake the Hushmen for a day.
plays.consequence: No bargain is offered, so no favor is owed. The Court watches them closely.
plays.later: S8: Maudrin's last word still comes, through Isolde. S23: with no favor owed, Maudrin runs the Strike normally.
plays.fallback: If they wander, Lysse Carrow drops a bone-bound book at their feet in the street and asks them to carry it back to the Archive.
plays.keywords: refuse invitation, skip assembly, don't go, avoid maudrin, stay away, rook, wren, investigation, lysse

plays.title: They accept Maudrin's bargain for Ossa's Tongue
plays.why: Safe passage, a pension and a protected memory are a real offer, and some players are tired of being hunted.
plays.tells: A player asks exactly what the exemption covers, or looks at the bundle and then at the others.
plays.readAloud: “Safe passage. A Court pension. And one memory of your choosing that no Tithe will ever touch.” Maudrin folds her grey gloves. “All I ask is the thing your friend is carrying, which was never yours to carry.”
plays.response: Maudrin keeps her word about exactly what she promised. Each character names one memory on a grey card she signs: no Court Tithe can take it (Tolls, the stairs of the Hush and eel bites are not Tithes). She calls Ser Haldric, 'my dear' — and corrects it to 'Ser' before the word is finished. Haldric carries the Tongue to the Dawn Order armory beside Vaer's Tongue, so the party sees a Dawn Order knight take the Chancellor's orders. The pension is 5 gp a month for Stormborn (she knows they prefer gold) or 5 keeps for Corvanese.
plays.rules: Influence DC 17 (Maudrin's Intelligence) to haggle a better term, such as Ila's exemption too. Record in the Bargain Log: one favor owed.
plays.consequence: Ossa's Tongue is in the Dawn Order armory. The party owes Maudrin one favor.
plays.later: S6: if Rook wins the hearing, she takes the armory and hands Ossa's Tongue back to the party (s06-rook-returns-ossa). S9: or they steal it with Vaer's (s09-steal-ossa-too). S23: Maudrin calls the favor in on the ridge: 'One favor, dear, and I am calling it in now. Go, before I change my mind.'
plays.fallback: If the table splits, Maudrin gives them until the end of the masque and dances with Isolde while they argue.
plays.keywords: accept, bargain, deal, maudrin, exemption, pension, safe passage, hand over, give tongue, favor, ossa

plays.title: They refuse Maudrin's bargain
plays.why: Most tables have decided by now that the Court is the problem.
plays.tells: Players answer with a question about the Tithe, or say no outright.
plays.readAloud: Her smile does not move at all. “Then the Assembly will go on without you. Enjoy the city.”
plays.response: She does not threaten. Two Hushmen follow the party for the rest of the Act at a polite distance; a DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth) group check loses them for a day, and they are back next morning. Isolde Drave finds the party within the hour, delighted: people who refuse Maudrin are the most interesting people in the room. A locket at her throat holds a boy's portrait; she closes it when someone looks. For one true story about the Mere, Isolde trades one true secret: 'The Tithe-Ledger Room has a service passage, and a Hushman named Ilam Bray walks past it every evening.' She also mentions, idly, that Ironhorn bronze is cheaper this year.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 15 to shake the tail (once a day). Isolde: Influence DC 15, Indifferent; clever talk makes her Friendly. Record in the Bargain Log: refused.
plays.consequence: No favor is owed. The Court watches them, and Isolde is curious.
plays.later: S5: the Ledger shows Isolde's Ironhorn sales (s05-take-ledger). S7: the Ilam Bray lead pays off. S8: Maudrin's last word is warmer than they expect, and Isolde can be turned (s08-turn-isolde).
plays.fallback: If they freeze, Maudrin answers the question nobody asked: 'Yes, I know about your Tongue. Everyone does.'
plays.keywords: refuse, no deal, decline, reject bargain, maudrin, hushmen follow, tail, isolde, gossip

plays.title: They tell Maudrin where the Tongue is
plays.why: The party no longer carries Ossa's Tongue, so Maudrin changes the bargain: “Then tell me where it is, and you will be rewarded.”
plays.tells: The Tongue is with Master Venn or beyond the Seam, and a player starts weighing the pension.
plays.readAloud: “Then you don't have it.” Maudrin smiles as if you have passed a test. “Tell me where it is, and you will be rewarded. Lie to me and I'll know by morning, which would be a waste of both our evenings.”
plays.response: She wants a place, not a promise, and the truth costs whoever holds it. On Venn's Gilded Heron or gone through the Seam: the Court seizes Venn's cargo at the Landing House, and Venn learns who told. Telling her earns the pension and exemption, and the favor. If the Tongue is with Ila, play s04-tell-where-ila.
plays.rules: Deception against Maudrin's Insight (+4); anything the Court's records contradict fails automatically. Record in the Bargain Log: one favor owed.
plays.consequence: The party owes Maudrin a favor, and whoever holds the Tongue is in danger.
plays.later: S23: the favor is called in on the ridge. If they named Venn, he treats them as enemies on their return to Pellmoor.
plays.fallback: If they won't say, play s04-bargain-refuse.
plays.keywords: tell, reveal, where is it, location, inform, maudrin, ila, venn, dawn order, armory, reward

plays.title: They take Maudrin's exemption for Ila
plays.why: Maudrin already holds Ossa's Tongue (S3), so she bargains for the girl who heard it.
plays.tells: Players ask about Ila, or whether the arrest order can be withdrawn.
plays.readAloud: “I have the Tongue. You were very sensible.” Maudrin turns her glass in her fingers. “The girl who heard it, though. Ila. My office has an order for her. I could lose it, and give her the same exemption I'd give you. For a favor.”
plays.response: This is the only bargain she has to offer. Ila is free or hidden, so Maudrin tears the arrest order in half in front of them. The party owes the favor. If they refuse, the order stands and Hushmen move on Ila within two days.
plays.rules: Influence DC 17 to add anything to the deal. Record in the Bargain Log: one favor owed.
plays.consequence: Ila is safe from the Court's Tithe for now. The party owes Maudrin a favor.
plays.later: S23: the favor is called in, and Maudrin reminds them who it was for. S28: Ila, untithed, grows up to keep the ledger and to ring the ferry-folk's bell.
plays.fallback: If the party argues morality with her, she agrees with every word and keeps the order in her hand.
plays.keywords: ila, exemption, arrest order, release, protect ila, maudrin, favor, bargain, child

plays.title: Ossa's Tongue went back to the Mere
plays.why: The Tongue is at the Ossa Belfry (S3), so there is nothing to bargain for, and Maudrin knows it.
plays.tells: Maudrin greets them without asking for anything.
plays.readAloud: “You put it back.” Maudrin says it gently, as if she were sorry for them. “Every glass in my palace hummed that night. I had them all wrapped in cloth.”
plays.response: Skip the bargain. She asks, with real curiosity, what the bell sounded like, and listens to the answer. She offers one smaller deal from Part 9: a Court pension in exchange for their silence about what they found under the Mere; accepting it means they owe her the favor. If Ossa was rung, she says the Court will 'revisit Pellmoor's quota in the spring', which means the collectors have withdrawn for now.
plays.rules: Influence DC 17 if they want anything else from her. Insight DC 15: she is relieved the Tongue is not in the city.
plays.consequence: No Tongue changes hands. Maudrin has measured them.
plays.later: S23: a favor is owed only if they took the pension. Act V: Ossa's resonance persists for the Concord whatever the Court does to Pellmoor.
plays.fallback: If the table wants a fight with her, she introduces them to Isolde and leaves.

plays.title: They find Brother Eld among the guests
plays.why: An exposed or forgiven Eld came to Hallowmere and serves as a Court chaplain at the masque.
plays.tells: A player scans the room for familiar faces, or asks who the chaplain is.
plays.readAloud: A tall, round-shouldered man in chaplain's grey stands by the punch with his mask slightly crooked. Ink still on his fingers. He sees you, and his face does the sad thing it was trained to do.
plays.response: If Eld fled in disgrace, he will not meet their eyes; cornered behind a pillar, he begs them not to tell anyone what he did, and buys their silence with the name of the Court's new Pellmoor informer, a ferry-boy called Coll who owes the Landing House money. If they forgave him, he meets their eyes and slips a folded hymn-sheet into a pocket as he passes: 'Your names came up the river in Quill's report. Ser Haldric carried it to the palace, not to the Order.'
plays.rules: Influence DC 15: Friendly if forgiven, Hostile with fear if exposed. Intimidation works on a frightened Eld and sends him running to Haldric.
plays.consequence: The party has an informant (forgiven) or a frightened man who owes them his secret (fled).
plays.later: S6: Eld's note is a corroborating witness that Haldric serves the palace, though not proof of payment. S28: Eld confesses publicly, dies in the Mere, or leaves forever, following how they treat him now.
plays.fallback: If they ignore him, a forgiven Eld finds them at the door with the same note; a disgraced one avoids them all night.
plays.keywords: eld, brother eld, chaplain, priest, informant, ledger page, pellmoor, mask, note, haldric

plays.title: They threaten Maudrin at the masque
plays.why: A frustrated or bold player decides the villain is right there and lightly guarded.
plays.tells: Hands on hilts, a raised voice, a spell component in a fist.
plays.readAloud: She laughs, softly, delighted. “Oh, you're adorable. Haldric, please see to our guests.”
plays.response: Ser Haldric Mose arrives with four palace guards: a Dawn Order knight answering the Chancellor's call is the surprise. Maudrin says 'Haldric, please see to our guests' and, as he passes, touches his sleeve: 'my boy', and then 'Ser'. He asks them to leave, courteously, twice. If they fight, use Haldric's Escort; Maudrin leaves by a side door and casts only if someone casts at her (Counterspell). Nobody dies at the masque: guests scream, guards grapple, and anyone dropped wakes in Vaer's Belfry.
plays.rules: Haldric's silence-stone shield negates the first spell that targets only him each day. Maudrin: Counterspell (3/day). Grappled, Prone. A knock-out is the default for every Court combatant.
plays.consequence: The party is a named enemy, and they have seen Haldric take the Chancellor's orders.
plays.later: S6: 'Who called you to the masque, Ser Haldric?' is a fair question on the Dawn Steps, though not proof of payment. S6: Rook says Haldric came to the Order at twelve with a palace letter. S23: Maudrin remembers this evening when she makes her offer on the ridge.
plays.fallback: If it starts to go badly, Isolde steps between them with a fresh glass and a joke, and the guards take the hint.
plays.keywords: threaten, attack maudrin, kill, assassinate, fight, masque, haldric, guards, violence, intimidate

plays.title: They mention a key that can ring the Seventh
plays.why: Players who picked up rumours from Eld's papers, a Mere Memory or a Bellwright may test Maudrin with it.
plays.tells: A player asks about 'the Key' or 'the Seventh Bell' by name.
plays.readAloud: Her face goes still for half a second, the way the Mere goes still. Then she says, quite pleasantly, “I have no idea what you mean,” and turns to thank the musicians.
plays.response: The Assembly ends early: the music stops, Hushmen open the doors, and guests are thanked for coming. Maudrin does not look at the party again tonight. By the time they reach their lodgings, two Hushmen stand at the door and their Tithe records are flagged.
plays.rules: Insight DC 15 catches the half-second: she was afraid, not angry.
plays.consequence: The party is the Court's enemy.
plays.later: S8: her last word mentions the Key outright; she has stopped pretending. S13: the Sexton will tell them what she was afraid of. Part 9, Situation 4: the Key stays in her palace vault until she leaves Hallowmere.
plays.fallback: If nobody pushes further, Isolde catches them on the stairs and says, 'Whatever you said, say it to me next time.'

plays.title: They read Maudrin with Insight, Detect Thoughts or Zone of Truth
plays.why: She is the antagonist, and casters reach for mind magic the moment she speaks.
plays.tells: A player asks “Is she lying?” or quietly names a spell.
plays.readAloud: Your spell hums behind your teeth. Across the table Maudrin's eyes flick to you, then to your lips, and she smiles as though you had complimented her dress.
plays.response: Every spell in Corvane hums as it is cast, and Maudrin hears it. Detect Thoughts on her surface mind gives: 'Four of them. Ossa's. Not yet.' If the caster probes deeper she saves at +4; on a failure the caster sees a grey case on a chain, hears a lullaby, and feels her fear, and either way she knows, says “That was rude,” and ends the conversation. Zone of Truth fails near her chair: two silence-stones sit in the plinths of the dais, and the dimmed light shows the boundary before anyone casts. Insight DC 15 without magic tells them she means every promise and is leaving something out.
plays.rules: Detect Thoughts (2nd level; Maudrin's Wisdom save +4). Silence-stone field, 10 feet (Part 2.6 house rule). Insight DC 15. Maudrin's Counterspell is an NPC ability. See any-l3-truth-and-minds for the campaign-wide ruling.
plays.consequence: They know she fears something she carries. She knows they read people.
plays.later: S22: the grey case and the lullaby make sense. S23: her first Counterspell goes to whoever cast Detect Thoughts on her tonight.
plays.fallback: If no one has the spell, Insight alone gives the same last sentence.
plays.keywords: detect thoughts, zone of truth, insight, read her, mind, lie, spell, probe, truth, silence-stone, dais

plays.title: They pay the Librarian for the diary's label
plays.why: The Librarian offers the answer outright for one true memory, and Edda's diary is the Act's prize.
plays.tells: A player opens the wordless book, or asks Lysse where to look.
plays.readAloud: The pages show your own face, then fill with handwriting that is almost yours: “You have asked a question with a memory behind it. Edda Thorne's diary is not on any shelf of this archive. Ask me the label, and I will tell you it, for one true memory.”
plays.response: The price is a memory the player is willing to give; the player names it and writes it in the ledger as a trade with the Librarian (not a Toll, not a Tithe, never redeemable). Never from an absent player's character. The answer is true: MIREL, LOST. Each further question costs another memory and gets a true but partial answer. If nobody will pay, the clue is not lost: Lysse cross-checks the Archive's accession lists and finds a Court receipt for 'one diary, relabelled'.
plays.rules: Study action, Intelligence (Investigation) DC 15 for Lysse's shortcut in an hour; on a failure she finds it by morning. Record Librarian trades as their own kind in the ledger.
plays.consequence: They know what to look for in the vault: a cloth-wrapped book labelled MIREL, LOST.
plays.later: S5: they find the diary in a minute once inside. S22: if every other source is gone, the Librarian reads the Quiet Night page aloud for one true memory.
plays.fallback: If the table stalls on the price, Lysse offers to pay it herself, and does; she has very little left to lose, and that should sting.
plays.keywords: librarian, sealed book, sealed stacks, question, label, diary, edda, mirel lost, memory, price, lysse

plays.title: They bargain for Mirel's Tongue
plays.why: The Librarian holds Mirel's Tongue and will trade it now, which saves the courier's bargain at Vael Tor.
plays.tells: A player asks what else the Librarian keeps, or whether it would trade for a Tongue.
plays.readAloud: A page turns by itself. “I keep the dream-bell's tongue because it belongs to whoever read it last. Give me a dream you have never told anyone, and you will be the last.”
plays.response: The price is a dream the giver has never told anyone; it is gone for good, and the player tells you (privately if they like) what it was. Never from an absent player's character. If they refuse the dream, the Librarian accepts a Gift instead (Part 2.7): something the giver values, given freely and never returned. The Tongue is a honey-coloured bronze clapper the length of a forearm, warm, and anyone who holds it yawns.
plays.rules: Record the dream as a Librarian trade, or the Gift as a Gift. Neither is Mirel's Toll: a Fear for one day is still owed when Mirel rings.
plays.consequence: The party carries Mirel's Tongue.
plays.later: S16B or S20: they can ring Mirel as soon as they reach the Sleeping Hall, and the Librarian's courier never comes. S9: a cart search at the north gate is now a real danger. S23: Maudrin wants every Tongue they carry.
plays.fallback: If they refuse both prices, tell them plainly that the courier will repeat the offer at Vael Tor.
plays.keywords: mirel, tongue, dream, librarian, trade, gift, bargain, dream bell, sleeping hall, buy

plays.title: They steal Mirel's Tongue from the Sealed Stacks
plays.why: A dream nobody has told is a steep price, and rogues like a reading stand with nothing guarding it.
plays.tells: A player asks where exactly the Tongue sits, or whether the book can see.
plays.readAloud: The Tongue rests on a reading stand between two shelves, under a page that has written, very small: 'Do not.'
plays.response: Lifting it unseen is DC 16 Dexterity (Stealth) to reach the stand, or DC 16 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) with Thieves' Tools to free it from the stand's clasp. Success: they have it, and the Librarian writes 'Then you are the last who read me' and closes; it answers no more questions this visit. Failure: the book slams, every warm spine in the Archive goes cold, and the Librarian fights only if someone keeps grabbing (The Librarian). The reading-room keepers fetch Hushmen in ten minutes, not three rounds.
plays.rules: Stealth or Thieves' Tools DC 16. The Stacks are not silence-stone: spells work, but hum loudly in the quiet, and the Librarian hears them.
plays.consequence: On a success the party holds Mirel's Tongue and the Librarian is cold to them; on a failure the Tongue stays.
plays.later: S16B: if the theft failed, the courier still comes with the same offer. S22: even a cold Librarian keeps its word and reads the Quiet Night page for one true memory.
plays.fallback: If they fail and flee, Lysse covers for them with the keepers, and asks what on earth they were thinking.

plays.title: They break into the vault with tools or spells
plays.why: Lockpicks and Knock are the first tools most parties reach for.
plays.tells: A player asks about the lock, guards, or whether Knock or Invisibility will work.
plays.readAloud: The vault door is grey stone banded in iron. Ten feet out, the lamplight dims and there is a pressure in your ears like diving. Whatever hums behind your teeth goes quiet.
plays.response: The lock is DC 17 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) with Thieves' Tools; a failure costs a minute. A Hushman passes every ten minutes (DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth) to wait in shadow). Fixed silence-stones in the frame and walls cover the door and the whole room: Knock fails, Invisibility and Pass without Trace are suppressed inside (they resume outside if concentration holds). Prying a frame stone loose (AC 12, 10 HP) ends the field at the door, but stone cracking on stone sets off the alarm.
plays.rules: Thieves' Tools DC 17. Stealth DC 15. Silence-stone house rule (Part 2.6): no spell can be cast in the field or produce an effect inside it. A fixed stone: AC 12, 10 HP. Misty Step cast from outside lands you at the edge of the field, not inside; Disguise Self and Invisibility drop at the threshold. Dispel Magic (an NPC's, or Aurelie's) cannot target a stone because it is not a spell.
plays.consequence: They are in, and no Tonework works anywhere in the vault.
plays.later: S7: Ilam Bray's service-passage key makes a second visit easy. Act IV (Situation 21): coming back for anything left on these shelves means this door again, with the Tithe Clock running.
plays.fallback: If the lock beats them, Ansel comes out of the service passage with a lamp and a very guilty look.

plays.title: They open a memory jar of their own

plays.tells: A player searches the shelves for their name.
plays.readAloud: The jar has a name on it in a clerk's tidy hand. It is warm. When you lift the stopper, the vault fills with a smell you had forgotten you knew.
plays.response: Ask the player first whether their character grew up under the Court. If so, their earliest-memory jar is here: describe it from the character's earliest years and ask the player to add one detail; it is theirs again. Offer a clue as a question, not a fact: the clerk who drew it wore a Hushman's grey glove, and the date is a Tithe-raid year. Ask whether the character's family ever spoke of it. Never invent a backstory loss without the player. A Stormborn character, or one who arrived this week, has no childhood jar: they have only the S4 courtesy jar, which opens the same way. Ansel's office tallies the jars each morning, so the empty one tells the Court who has been in.
plays.rules: Opening one's own jar restores the memory (Tithe, redeemable). Opening another person's jar only witnesses it and fades it; after three strangers it is spent. The S4 courtesy jar is on the newest shelf.

Read the full Quiet Night entry aloud (S5 box). Taking it sets off no alarm; the Court knows it has gone by morning. If they would rather not risk it, they can read it and leave it: set the diary to 'Read and left behind', and the Court never learns.

plays.response: The alarm is mechanical, not Tonework, so it works inside the silence-stone: the shelf is weighted, and any lift pulls the bell. A clever swap (an equal weight, DC 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand)) delays it by ten minutes instead of three rounds, but it still sounds. Hushmen arrive in three rounds (Vault Alarm), so the party should be moving by round two. For the next two days, four Hushmen search every cart leaving the city.

Failure alerts the guards and starts a chase through the lanes, never an automatic Tithe (Tessa's Guards). Bet Ostrow hides Tessa overnight above the bakery and Wren has a cart out at dawn.

plays.title: They calm the crowd (it works)
plays.why: Hundreds of grieving people and a line of Hushmen: most parties try words first.
plays.tells: A player climbs onto something to be seen, or asks who leads the crowd.
plays.readAloud: The Hall of Tithes is surrounded. Hundreds of people, grey-faced, holding up old drawings and wooden toys, shouting names they cannot quite remember. They do not riot. They only stand and ask, over and over, “Who was she? Who was I?” The Hushmen are forming a line.
plays.response: The Blanks follow anyone who promises to help them recover their memories, and they hold that person to it. Calming them is Influence (Persuasion) DC 16 by one speaker, with Help from others; a promise backed by something real (jars from the vault, the Ledger's names) gives advantage. On a success the crowd sits down on the steps in silence, which the Hushmen have no procedure for, and Sergeant Orla Gaunt orders the line to hold. If the roll fails, play s07-calm-crowd-fails.
plays.rules: Influence DC 16 for the crowd; Help gives advantage. Calm Emotions or Thaumaturgy can also give advantage (see s07-spells-crowd).
plays.consequence: The Blanks trust the party, and expect them to keep their promise.
plays.later: S22: the Blanks march. S23: they break the Hushmen's line by numbers. S28–30: every promise made on these steps is asked about by name.
plays.fallback: If the speech stalls, a Blank at the front asks the speaker their name, forgets it, and asks again; the crowd laughs, and the tension breaks a little.

plays.title: They fight the Hushmen line
plays.why: The line moves on unarmed grieving people; many tables will not stand by.
plays.tells: Weapons out, or a player steps between a Hushman and a Blank.
plays.readAloud: Six grey gloves come up together. Where they strike, there is no sound at all, and that is the worst part.
plays.response: The Hushmen want arrests, not deaths, and so do the Blanks: area damage near the crowd hits Blanks too (Commoners, 4 HP each). Use the Hushmen Line. Give the party a way to end it fast: Sergeant Gaunt withdraws when half her line is down or the party holds the Hall's doors. Afterward the steps belong to the Blanks, and to the party.
plays.rules: Hushmen: Pack Tactics, grapple. Silence-stone gloves silence only their own strikes. Blanks are Commoners (4 HP).
plays.consequence: The party is the Blanks' champion and the Court's named enemy.
plays.later: S9: the north gate is reinforced (Gate Sweep at every gate). S22: the Blanks march. S23: they break the line by numbers.
plays.fallback: If it turns bloody, Captain Rook's knights arrive on the far side of the square and the Sergeant decides she has been outnumbered.

plays.title: They reunite Jonah and Ilam Bray
plays.why: A boy with a wooden bird and a Hushman who stops when he sees it: the scene asks to be finished.
plays.tells: A player notices Ilam staring at the bird, or asks Jonah where he got it.
plays.readAloud: “That's my carving. I made it for my son. I don't know his name anymore. I've tried. I don't know why I can't remember. Is he in there? In the crowd? Please. I need to see him.”
plays.response: Bring Jonah to the edge of the line, or Ilam to the boy. Neither remembers the other's name. The bird does it: Ilam turns it over, finds the notch where his knife slipped, and Jonah says, very literally, “You made that.” Ilam takes off his silence-stone gloves on the spot and drops them on the stones. He gives the party a key to the Tithe-Ledger Room's service passage and the Hushman roster: every name, post and shift.
plays.rules: No check if Jonah trusts the party (he attaches to whoever is kind). Stealth DC 13 to get Ilam out of the line before his Sergeant notices.
plays.consequence: Ilam deserts the Hushmen. The party holds a vault key and the roster.
plays.later: S9: the roster says which gate and shift to avoid. S22: Ilam holds the Tor's southern road. S23: Ilam stands between Jonah and the fight, and Jonah sees his father clearly. S30: Jonah remembers his mother's face, if she is found.

plays.title: They use magic on the crowd or the line
plays.why: Calm Emotions, Suggestion and Silence are all on level 3–4 lists and all look made for this square.
plays.tells: A caster asks how many people a spell can cover, or whether the Sergeant can be charmed.
plays.readAloud: Your spell hums across the square, and every grey glove in the line turns toward the sound.
plays.response: Calm Emotions on the crowd's front ranks gives advantage on the DC 16 Influence and ends Frightened in the area. Suggestion on Sergeant Gaunt ('send your men home; there's nothing to arrest here') works if she fails her Wisdom save; she obeys and is furious afterward. The Silence spell over the line is sacramental here: the Hushmen hesitate for one round, because nobody has ever turned the Court's holy quiet against them. Thaumaturgy lets one speaker be heard across the whole square.
plays.rules: Calm Emotions (Charisma save, unwilling only). Suggestion (Gaunt's Wisdom save +2). Silence the spell is not silence-stone: Tonework works outside its sphere. Lesser Restoration does not restore Tithed memories. Every spell hums, so the line knows who cast.
plays.consequence: Magic can win the crowd a night. The caster is marked.
plays.later: S9: the caster's description is at every gate, with +2 to the DC of any bluff there.
plays.fallback: If a spell fails, the hum alone makes the front rank of Blanks turn and look at the caster with hope, which is pressure enough.

plays.title: They trace the courier
plays.why: A shaking one-line letter from 'I.V.' begs the question who carried it.
plays.tells: A player asks where the courier went, or who paid him.
plays.readAloud: The courier is a trapper in reindeer hide with frost-burn on both cheeks, and he will not sit near the fire. “Not mine to explain,” he says. “I was paid to carry it. The sister wrote it. The voice said it.”
plays.response: He is Edrin Moss, a Glassreach trapper. A DC 16 Intelligence (Investigation) check, or a drink and Influence DC 15, gets the rest: he was paid by Wyn Talla, an old woman at the forest's edge whose family has watched the glass for four hundred years. They call the woman in it 'the sister'. A voice in the glass told Wyn what to write, called itself 'I.V.', and promised the sister would move again. On a failure Edrin leaves at dawn and they can follow his tracks north. That afternoon two Hushmen and a Court agent try to take Edrin off the street (Courier Snatch): Isolde wants to read the letter too.
plays.rules: Investigation DC 15, or Influence DC 15 (Edrin is Indifferent; Friendly if paid or warmed).
plays.consequence: They know where to start in Glassreach (Wyn Talla's hut, beside Yara's camp) and that the Court is interested.
plays.later: S10: Wyn waits at Yara's camp and asks them to free the woman in the glass (s10-meet-wyn). S11: Maren Talla is one of the Stilled adults; waking her gently is the kind route. S15: if Maren wakes, Wyn is first to bring the Stilled bread.

plays.title: They question Isolde about Maudrin's last word

plays.tells: Players ask what 'he was once family' means, or what the Key is.
plays.readAloud: “Thank you for your curiosity. It is, after all, why I invited you. When you come back from the north, I will be waiting, and so will the Key. Give my regards to the Glass Sexton. He was once family, and he will not thank you for disturbing him.”
plays.response: Isolde reads it word for word and watches what it does to their faces. Asked what it means, she gives the truth as she knows it: the Glass Sexton is Imber Vesk, High Sexton on the Quiet Night, and 'once family' means exactly that. She does not know what the Key is, and that bothers her. She mentions, idly, that the North Road is cold and that she has never liked the cold.
plays.rules: Insight DC 15: she is going north herself, and isn't pleased about it. Influence DC 15 (Isolde's Intelligence 12) to learn when: within a day of their leaving.
plays.consequence: They know the Sexton is a Vesk, and that someone will follow them north.
plays.later: S9: Isolde follows with a Hushman escort (s09-isolde-follows). S12: the Sexton asks who rules the Court, and the answer is his own blood. S15: Isolde arrives at the thaw.

plays.title: They turn Isolde into an informant

plays.tells: A player brings up her son, or what she sells and to whom.

Either moves her to Friendly; then Influence DC 15 seals it. She will still be sent north, because refusing would expose her, but she brings only two Hushmen and warns the party what the Court wants.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15, only after a real offer or real leverage. Record in the Bargain Log: Isolde's son's safety.
plays.consequence: Isolde is their informant inside the Court, for as long as it protects her son.
plays.later: S9: she follows anyway, leaving a note at the first waystation naming her escort (s09-isolde-follows-ally). S15: she asks for the Frost Tongue in front of her Hushmen, then offers a private way to 'lose' it (s15-isolde-informant). S21: she warns them a day before Maudrin leaves Hallowmere.

plays.title: They ring Vaer

plays.tells: A player asks what Vaer would do, or what it costs.

Then state the Toll and wait for a yes: a memory of a dawn you loved; a Corvanese character raised in Hallowmere who never saw one may offer a memory of a hoped-for beginning instead. If they decline, the bell does not ring and no Toll is taken. When it rings, the Court marks the Ringer with a Silence Warrant. If Sister Aurelie is in the city, she is on the terraces singing to Lathander within the hour (s09-aurelie-on-the-terraces).

Bet Ostrow is the natural recipient if she is with her own free choice (she is eighty and decides for herself whether to travel three days); otherwise the innkeeper of the Empty Sheaf has six children and one coat. Nessa Harrow, Ila's mother, lives here: she comes out to look at the green fields, and if anyone says Ila's name, she sits down in the ash. Afterward, Court Tithe-men raid the Crossing for the rest of the season and try to capture the Ringer; play that out, don't assume it.

plays.title: Isolde follows them north
plays.why: Isolde failed to keep them in the city; the Court sends her after them.
plays.tells: The party notices the same carriage twice, or a player asks if they're being followed.
plays.readAloud: Two days out, a carriage with grey curtains stops at the same waystation you do. Nobody gets out. In the morning it is a mile behind you, and it stays a mile behind you.
plays.response: Isolde follows with two Hushmen (four if they fought their way out) to see what they find in the north. Spotting her is DC 15 Wisdom (Perception or Survival). They can confront her (she is charming and admits everything except her orders), lose her (Pass without Trace and a DC 15 group Survival check off the road), or ignore her. Losing her only delays her: she knows from the letter where they are going. Capturing her is s09-capture-isolde.
plays.rules: Perception or Survival DC 15 to notice. Group Survival DC 15 to lose her for two days.
plays.consequence: The Court has eyes on the party all the way to Glassreach.
plays.later: S15: Isolde arrives at the thaw with her escort; if they lost her, she arrives two days late, cold and angry, after the Spire is rung. If they capture her on the road, the Court sends Tristan Vesk in her place.
plays.fallback: If nobody looks back, Isolde sends a bottle of warm wine to their table at the second waystation, with her compliments.
plays.keywords: followed, tail, isolde, carriage, spy, chase, lose her, ambush, confront, north road

plays.title: They lie low until the searches stop
plays.why: Waiting out a two-day search is the sensible option, if the city lets them.
plays.tells: “We hide for a couple of days.”
plays.readAloud: Two days of grey light through an attic window, and boots in the street below at odd hours. Bet brings up bread and doesn't ask.
plays.response: Two nights in Bet's attic, the Dawn Mission's cellar, or Rook's barracks. The cart searches end after two days. Each night is a Tithe Clock tick; at 6 the Court sweeps the city and puts a checkpoint on every road, which makes the wait self-defeating. Use the time: the Hallowmere Ledger questions, a last visit to Lysse, Ilam finding Jonah.
plays.rules: Tithe Clock +2. At 6: Hushmen sweep, checkpoints on every road (Gate Sweep at every gate). Rest in an attic is safe; Misty Step is blocked by silence-stone streets once the clock hits 12.
plays.consequence: The searches end. The Court's clock moves.
plays.later: S10: the Tithe Clock resets after a week outside Court cities. If it hits 12 before they leave, silence-stones go into every street; they stay even after the party is gone, waiting for any return in Act IV.
plays.fallback: If the clock is already near 6, Bet says plainly, 'You can't stay. They're counting.'
plays.keywords: hide, lie low, wait, rest, attic, safe house, searches, delay, tithe clock

plays.title: They go back to Pellmoor before heading north
plays.why: Ila, Ossa's bell, Venn's export trade or Aurelie's mission pull some tables back to the Mere before Glassreach.
plays.tells: Players talk about Ila, Venn, or ringing Ossa with a recovered Tongue.
plays.readAloud: The Quays are louder than you remember. Forty masts, no gulls, and on the Tally's slate the day's rate: 1 KEEP = 1 GP 2 SP. Someone has chalked underneath it: HOW MUCH FOR A MOTHER?
plays.response: Pellmoor is three days by ferry and road, and Glassreach is then about two weeks away. With Ossa's Tongue in hand, the Tidewarden ferries the Ringer to the Ossa Belfry and his air pocket gets them down (s09-ring-ossa-later). Water Breathing is a 3rd-level spell they will not have until level 5. Venn's counting-house holds the other half of the EXPORT column, and confronting him in public makes him their enemy and moves the Landing (any-confront-venn). The Harper cellar (s01-brass-lantern) and the Dawn Mission (s01-dawn-mission) are a short walk away. Reckoner Sela Maunt can tell exported keeps by their wax stamps.
plays.rules: Ossa's Toll: a memory of someone who has died. Holding breath lasts 1 + Constitution modifier minutes. Set Venn to 'Exposed, now hostile' if they confront him publicly.
plays.consequence: The north waits. Pellmoor's threads tighten.
plays.later: S22: the Stormborn ally (Harper agents, the Dawn Mission, or a Baldurian crew) is earned here if they exposed Venn or protected the ferry-folk. S15: Isolde follows them to Pellmoor and north again; only the days change.
plays.fallback: If the detour stalls, Brannagh Wick tells them the Seam is narrowing for the season and Venn's last ship sails in four days.

plays.title: They settle accounts before the road
plays.why: Every Act II choice needs to be on record before Act III, and the players enjoy the recap.
plays.tells: The party reaches the north gate, or asks 'What did we leave undone?'
plays.readAloud: The North Road runs up out of the city between grey hedges, and the Dawn Order's watchtower falls behind you. Ahead, the land rises toward the Ninefold hills. Somewhere behind, a single bell tolls once, muffled by the cloud, and then falls silent.
plays.response: Ask the seven Hallowmere Ledger questions aloud and let the players answer: the jar, Rook or Haldric, Jonah and Ilam, Maudrin's bargain, the diary, the Tongues, Tessa. Set the matching flags in Foresight as they answer. Then ask which unfinished promise they carry north, and write it as a Bargain Log line.
plays.rules: Level the party to 5 once Hallowmere is resolved.
plays.consequence: Your state is correct before Act III.
plays.later: Every answer is a later: S15 (Isolde, Tongues carried), S22 (allies: Dawn Order, Blanks, Ilam), S23 (Haldric present or absent, Jonah hostage or safe, Maudrin's favor).
plays.fallback: If the players don't remember something, it didn't happen; don't punish a forgotten thread.
plays.keywords: recap, summary, ledger, promises, questions, leave city, north road, level up, unfinished

plays.title: They push into the glass without proper gear
plays.why: Parties rarely pack for a winter that has lasted four hundred years.
plays.tells: Nobody mentions cloaks, or a player asks how cold it really is.
plays.readAloud: The cold here doesn't bite. It waits. After an hour your fingers stop telling you where they are, and your breath falls from your mouth as tiny stars that ring when they hit the ground.
plays.response: Glassreach is Extreme Cold. At the end of each hour, each creature makes a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or gains 1 Exhaustion level; Resistance or Immunity to Cold damage means automatic success, and so does a warm cloak or other cold-weather gear (house rule kept from v5). Each Exhaustion level is −2 to every d20 Test and −5 feet of Speed; a long rest removes one. Yara sells warm cloaks at her camp for 10 gp or a keep each, or trades one for a good tool. Telegraph it: the first failed save is a character's hands going white.
plays.rules: Extreme Cold (DMG 2024): DC 10 Constitution save hourly or 1 Exhaustion level. Warm cloak or Cold Resistance: automatic success. Exhaustion: −2 per level to d20 Tests, −5 ft Speed; long rest removes 1.
plays.consequence: Gear matters, and so does Yara.
plays.later: S11–S14: every hour in the glass is another save for anyone without a cloak; climbing the Spire at two Exhaustion levels is −4 on each Athletics check. S15: the woken Stilled need cloaks too.
plays.fallback: If a player is sliding toward a third level, Yara throws a cloak at them and puts it on their tab.
plays.keywords: cold, extreme cold, freeze, freezing, exhaustion, warm cloak, gear, frostbite, constitution, winter, glassreach

plays.title: They befriend Yara Thenn
plays.why: She sells what they need, knows every safe path, and is funny.
plays.tells: Players haggle, joke back, or ask about the Sexton.
plays.readAloud: “I'll tell you where the safe paths are. You tell me why you're going to the Sexton. Nobody goes to the Sexton for a pleasant chat. And if you're going to die, I'd like to know what for, so I can sell the story.”
plays.response: Yara sells glass-cutting tools (5 gp), warm cloaks and maps; she haggles constantly and prefers favours or good tools to coin. Befriending her needs honesty about the Sexton (Influence DC 15, with advantage if they tell her the truth). Friendly, she gives them the map of safe paths: advantage on Survival in Glassreach and no wandering Glass-Wolves on the marked paths. What she wants most is a map of the Frost Spire, because nobody has ever drawn one.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 (Yara starts Indifferent). Survival with her map: advantage.
plays.consequence: The party has safe paths and a guide who will come as far as the Stilled Clearing.
plays.later: S14: a friendly Yara shows them the old Sexton's stair on the north face (one fewer climbing check). S15: a sketch of the Spire drawn at the top earns her loyalty (s15-yara-map). S30: Yara finally opens her brother's glass-flower.
plays.fallback: If they insult her, she still sells them cloaks, at double price, and the map stays in her pocket.
plays.keywords: yara, thenn, scavenger, camp, map, safe paths, guide, haggle, buy, tools, cloaks

plays.title: They ask about the flower Yara won't sell
plays.why: Players notice the one thing a merchant refuses to price.
plays.tells: A player asks to buy it, or asks why she keeps it.
plays.readAloud: It sits in a felt-lined box: a single glass rose, and inside it something moves like a laugh caught in a jar. “That's not for sale,” Yara says, and shuts the box before you can see the colour.
plays.response: It holds a moment of her dead brother Teo's laugh, and she has never opened it because she is afraid it will shatter. It cannot be bought or stolen: if anyone tries, she closes the camp to them. If someone shares a true memory of their own grief with her, freely, she tells them about Teo and the winter that took him, and the giver earns Heroic Inspiration. A Bell-Touched character can tell her it will not shatter; that is true, and she does not believe it yet.
plays.rules: Heroic Inspiration for a memory given freely to someone who needs it (v6 generosity rule).
plays.consequence: Yara trusts them with the one thing she owns that matters.
plays.later: S15: as the thaw spreads, glass-flowers soften, and Yara has to decide whether to open hers before it melts. S30: she opens it.
plays.fallback: If they push, she says, 'Some things you keep because you can't afford what they cost,' and changes the subject to cloaks.
plays.keywords: glass-flower, flower, rose, brother, teo, laugh, not for sale, yara, buy, steal, grief

plays.title: They free the Stilled child
plays.why: A frozen child in a clearing is the clearest call to act in the forest.
plays.tells: A player kneels by the child, or asks whether she is alive.
plays.readAloud: “The man in the tower was sad. He sang to us so we wouldn't be afraid. Then he stopped singing, and the winter kept going, and we couldn't move anymore. Is it still winter out there?”
plays.response: The deer, the fox and the child stand mid-step in the Stilled Clearing. Cutting her free with glass-cutting tools is DC 14 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) and harms nothing; smashing it is DC 17 Strength and sends cracks into the deer and fox, which shatter and die. Any 20 Fire or Lightning damage to the glass melts it safely. She wakes, says her one true sentence, and freezes again within a minute; she does not attack. If child peril is Off-limits at your table, she is an old woman who was a child when the winter came.
plays.rules: Sleight of Hand DC 14 with glass-cutting tools, or Strength DC 17 to smash. 20 Fire or Lightning damage at the glass melts it.
plays.consequence: They know the Sexton once sang to the Stilled, and that the winter kept going when he stopped.
plays.later: S12: 'The man in the tower was sad' tells them he can be talked to. S15: after Hieme rings, she is among the first to wake for good, and she asks for her mother.
plays.fallback: If they won't touch her, Wyn Talla asks them to, because the woman in the glass she has kept watch over is three trees away and she needs to know it can be done.
plays.keywords: child, stilled child, girl, wake, free, break glass, cut, clearing, deer, fox, frozen

plays.title: A Faerûnian character recognises a Stilled sailor
plays.why: Some of the Stilled are Sword Coast sailors from before the Quiet Night, and a Stormborn character will know the cut of their coats.
plays.tells: A Faerûnian or a sailor looks closely at the Stilled at the clearing's edge.
plays.readAloud: Among the Stilled at the clearing's edge stands a man in a sea-coat cut four hundred years out of fashion, a brass badge on his breast: a ship under three stars, the old arms of a Tethyrian merchant house.
plays.response: A Sword Coast character recognises the badge with a DC 10 Intelligence (History) check; a sailor knows it outright. He is Bosun Corran Vell of the carrack Brightwater, out of Zazesspur, Stilled in 2 SS. Melted gently (fire at the glass, or Yara's tools), he wakes Hostile from shock but not violent at once; Influence DC 15 in Common calms him. He speaks an old dialect of Common, asks what year it is ('Is it still ten hundred and eighty-two?'), and says the Brightwater's crew are somewhere in these trees.
plays.rules: History DC 10. Influence DC 15 (Indifferent after a calm word). Comprehend Languages or Tongues helps with the old dialect, but any Common speaker gets the gist.
plays.consequence: The Stilled include Faerûnians. Someone from the Sword Coast came looking for the Ringing Land four centuries ago and never went home.
plays.later: S15: the Brightwater's crew wake with the thaw and want passage home through the Seam; getting them to Pellmoor earns a Stormborn ally for S22. S11: if not woken gently, Vell is one of the Stilled in the ambush.
plays.fallback: If no one is Faerûnian, Yara points at the badge: 'Loudfolk. Old ones. There's a dozen of them by the stream.'
plays.keywords: faerunian, stormborn, sailor, tethyr, zazesspur, badge, ship, brightwater, corran vell, old common, sword coast, year

plays.title: They leave the safe paths or split up
plays.why: The forest is beautiful, the Spire is visible, and the shortest line is never the safe one.
plays.tells: A player cuts across the glass, or the party splits to cover more ground.
plays.readAloud: A crack like a whip, somewhere to your left. Then a howl that rings, high and pure, the way a wineglass does when you run a wet finger round its rim.
plays.response: Off Yara's paths the glass is thin and the Glass-Wolves hunt by sound. Telegraph first with the crack and the howl, then run Off the Path: every wolf that shatters cracks the glass around nearby Stilled, and two of them wake. If the party split, cut between the groups and bring them together at the Stilled Clearing when the howling starts.
plays.rules: Survival DC 15 to keep to a path without Yara's map. Extreme Cold saves continue through the fight.
plays.consequence: The wolves are a warning; the woken Stilled are the real cost.
plays.later: S11: the two Stilled who woke angry remember who cracked them, and the ambush has two fewer sleepers in it. S15: Stilled harmed now are slower to trust.
plays.fallback: If the fight goes badly, Yara's whistle from the path draws the wolves off; glass-wolves hate a high, steady note.
plays.keywords: off path, shortcut, split up, wander, explore, wolves, glass-wolves, lost, separate, scout ahead

plays.title: They use fire, Shatter or Thunderwave in the glass
plays.why: Level-5 casters have Fireball, and a forest of glass looks like a problem fire solves.
plays.tells: A caster asks what fire does to the glass, or starts the incantation.
plays.readAloud: Yara grabs your wrist before the last word. “Not here. Not near them. You don't know what's inside the glass.”
plays.response: Be firm and say it before they cast: fire and lightning melt winter-moments, thunder shatters them. A Fireball in the clearing melts the glass around every Stilled in its area at once: the animals die, adults wake Hostile and in pain (they take the damage), and the child wakes and runs. Shatter or Thunderwave on a Stilled's glass breaks it with the person inside, who takes the damage and wakes screaming. Check session-zero Off-limits before the child is in the area. Every spell hums, so Yara hears it coming.
plays.rules: Fire or lightning damage to a winter-moment melts it; 20 damage over the scene frees someone peacefully, more than that hurts. Thunder damage shatters it and the Stilled inside takes the damage. Tell the player before they commit.
plays.consequence: Magic can wake the whole forest at once, but not gently.
plays.later: S11: an early Stilled Ambush. S15: the Stilled remember who woke them with fire, and their trust comes slower (stilled_trust is Wary).
plays.fallback: If they cast anyway, the waking adults run before they fight; give the party one round to choose calm or steel.
plays.keywords: fireball, fire, burn, melt, shatter, thunderwave, thunder, spell, glass, area spell, explode

plays.title: A character sees themselves in the glass
plays.why: This is the seed v5 plants for Act V; it happens to someone whether they look for it or not.
plays.tells: A player looks into a tall sheet of glass, or lingers alone.
plays.readAloud: In a sheet of glass as tall as a door you see yourself. Older. Grey at the temples. Holding a small dark key in both hands, and smiling.
plays.response: Choose the character whose story is most tied to the bells, or the player who looked first. Do not explain it. Ask the player, “What does your character feel?” and write the answer down word for word. If they break the glass, every shard shows the same thing.
plays.rules: No roll. Detect Magic shows nothing: it is not a spell.
plays.consequence: A seed for Act V. Nothing changes now.
plays.later: S26: the same figure stands at the foot of Ysh, older, holding the Key and smiling; read back what the player said here. S27: whether it was the Concord's Ringer or something else is the player's to decide.
plays.fallback: If nobody looks, the glass shows it to the character on watch that night.
plays.keywords: vision, reflection, glass, older self, key, smiling, mirror, future, winter-moment, h-18

plays.title: They damage the glass around a Stilled adult
plays.why: Waking the child worked; players try the same on the adults, or crack one by accident.
plays.tells: A hammer raised to an adult's glass, or a fight near the Stilled.
plays.readAloud: A crack runs up the glass like frost on a window. Inside, an eye moves. Then a hand. The man inside is screaming, and you cannot hear it until the glass breaks.
plays.response: Waking in pain and terror, an adult attacks whoever is closest, and the noise cracks the glass of others. Run the Stilled Ambush: they wake one or two a round, not all at once, so the party can see it growing and leave. A Stilled child does not attack; she speaks once and freezes again unless threatened. A Stilled who is spoken to mid-fight (Influence DC 15 as an action, in Hesk or old Common) stops, shaking, and becomes Indifferent.
plays.rules: Stilled Person (Gargoyle base): slow to start, hard to hurt through glass. Influence DC 15 as an action to calm one.
plays.consequence: Some Stilled are hurt or broken; some may be calmed.
plays.later: S15: Stilled who were calmed rather than shattered are the first to trust the party. S22: the Stilled walk to the Tor only if that trust is earned.
plays.fallback: If the fight turns grim, Maren Talla (if awake) stands in front of the next one and says its name.
plays.keywords: crack, break, hammer, wake, stilled, adult, ambush, attack, glass, fight

plays.title: They wake a Stilled adult slowly and kindly
plays.why: Wyn Talla wants her sister freed, and patient tables look for a way that isn't a hammer.
plays.tells: Players ask whether warmth or time would do it.
plays.readAloud: You wrap the glass in two cloaks and wait. It takes an hour. Water runs down the inside like tears, and then Maren Talla takes her first breath in four hundred and ten years.
plays.response: Melting with warmth over an hour (cloaks, a campfire, a held Produce Flame) or with glass-cutting tools (DC 14 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand)) wakes a Stilled without pain. They wake confused and Indifferent, not hostile; give them a name to hear and they listen. Maren asks what year it is. Wyn, her descendant, tells her, kneeling in the ash, and sings the family's thaw song; Maren knows the tune. Maren knows one useful thing: the Sexton's chapel is past the second frozen stream, and he cannot bear to be argued with.
plays.rules: An hour of warmth. Rescuers who gave up their cloaks make Extreme Cold saves. Sleight of Hand DC 14 with tools.
plays.consequence: One Stilled is free and grateful. Wyn has Maren back.
plays.later: S12: Maren's warning gives the party a free chance to stop arguing before the glass cracks. S15: Maren and Wyn lead the waking Stilled to Yara's camp, which counts toward the Stilled's trust.
plays.fallback: If nobody has the patience, Wyn sits down by the glass to do it herself, and the party has to decide whether to leave her there.
plays.keywords: gentle, melt, warm, slow, wake, maren, wyn, talla, sister, kind, careful, produce flame

plays.title: They slip past the Stilled without waking them
plays.why: Stealthy parties avoid fights with victims.
plays.tells: Players ask which paths avoid the clearing, or cast Pass without Trace.
plays.readAloud: You move between the frozen people like guests at a sleeping house. A wolf lifts its glass head somewhere in the trees, listens, and lowers it again.
plays.response: The Stilled act only when glass cracks; the Glass-Wolves are the danger. A group DC 13 Dexterity (Stealth) check gets everyone through; Yara's map gives advantage and Pass without Trace gives +10. On a failure, one wolf's howl cracks one Stilled's glass: a single adult wakes, not the full ambush, and the party can still leave.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 13; advantage with Yara's map; Pass without Trace +10.
plays.consequence: No fight, and no Stilled harmed.
plays.later: S14: the Spire's guard pack is the same pack; if it never saw them, the party has surprise at the Spire.
plays.fallback: If they fail, describe the single waking adult as confused first and angry second, and let them choose.
plays.keywords: sneak, stealth, avoid, slip past, pass without trace, quiet, careful, bypass

plays.title: They shatter Stilled or question the dead ones
plays.why: Treating the Stilled as monsters is quick, and a cleric with Speak with Dead wants answers.
plays.tells: A player goes for killing blows, or casts Speak with Dead on a broken body.
plays.readAloud: The glass comes apart in a sound like a chandelier falling. What was inside does not get up.
plays.response: Shattering a Stilled kills it; there is no reforming. Say so plainly the first time. Speak with Dead works on a shattered Stilled, since it is dead now: it remembers 2 SS, the first night of the winter, and a man in a tower singing so nobody would be afraid. The Stilled who remain remember who did the shattering.
plays.rules: Speak with Dead (3rd level; the party is level 5): five questions; the corpse knows only what it knew in life. A living Stilled is not a valid target. Tongues lets the speaker understand the old dialect.
plays.consequence: Lives ended, a little knowledge gained.
plays.later: S15: the Stilled don't trust the party if they shattered more than they saved (stilled_trust is Wary). S22: without that trust, the Stilled do not walk.
plays.fallback: If the table didn't realise the cost, let the next Stilled they approach flinch away from them.
plays.keywords: shatter, kill, destroy, break, stilled, speak with dead, question, corpse, dead

plays.title: They sit in the pews and listen
plays.why: He asks them to sit, he asks a question, and he has waited four centuries for an answer.
plays.tells: Players sit, or answer his question about the Court.
plays.readAloud: “Oh, look. Visitors. Children of the Court, I imagine. You carry the stink of memory-ink on your hands. Sit, please. I have waited so long to say something to someone who might understand. Who rules the Court now? I have not heard its name spoken in four centuries.”
plays.response: The Sexton does not attack unless the glass around him breaks or someone argues with him. He wants to be asked questions, and his first is his own. If they say Maudrin Vesk, he is silent a long time, then: “Vesk. Then it stayed in the family.” He will not explain until he has made his confession (S13). An hour of patient listening earns his trust: the confession begins without a check.
plays.rules: The Sexton starts Indifferent; patient listening makes him Friendly, no roll. Influence DC 15 otherwise.
plays.consequence: The Sexton has an audience at last, and he is ready to confess.
plays.later: S13: the 'listen patiently' route is already half done; he offers the Frost Tongue at the end of his confession (s13-listen-confession). S13: asked about the Key, he wants to know who holds it and the party has not yet told him; he asks again.
plays.fallback: If no one answers his question, he answers it himself: “Still a Vesk, I suppose. It always was.”
plays.keywords: listen, sit, pews, sexton, imber, sermon, question, who rules, court, maudrin, talk

plays.title: They resist the sermon's pull
plays.why: The sermon works on everyone in the chapel, and players want to know what it is doing to them.
plays.tells: A player asks why nobody is talking, or wants to shake it off.
plays.readAloud: “Quiet is the gift of the Silence. Memory is the burden of the living. Give your burdens up. Be still. Be at rest. There is no shame in forgetting.” After a while you realise you haven't spoken in some time, and that you don't especially want to.
plays.response: Each hour in the chapel, each listener makes a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure the character does not want to speak: they act and move freely and can talk if they choose, but have disadvantage on Charisma checks against the Sexton until they leave the chapel or finish a Short Rest. It never takes control of a character. In a fight the same sermon becomes his Sermon of Stillness (Charmed until the end of its next turn, Speed 0). Lost travelers (Hobb, a Kell's Crossing carter, and his two grown sons) sit in the pews and have not spoken in days; leading them out by the hand restores their voices within an hour.
plays.rules: Wisdom save DC 15, hourly. Failure: disadvantage on Charisma checks against the Sexton. Not the Charmed condition out of combat. In combat the Sermon is DC 15 and applies Charmed with Speed 0; Calm Emotions can suppress Charmed. Leaving the chapel ends the out-of-combat effect.
plays.consequence: The sermon is a pressure, not a prison.
plays.later: S13: in a fight the sermon becomes his Phase 1 ability (DC 15 Wisdom, Charmed until the end of its next turn). S15: Hobb's family carries news of the thaw south to Kell's Crossing.
plays.fallback: If the table finds it oppressive, let any character break the spell by saying a dead friend's name aloud.
plays.keywords: sermon, resist, wisdom, silence, quiet, charm, speak, voice, travelers, mute

plays.title: They argue with the Sexton
plays.why: The sermon says forgetting is a gift; players who have seen the Blanks will say no.
plays.tells: A player answers the sermon back, or calls him a liar.
plays.readAloud: The word goes up into the vaults like a stone thrown at a window. The glass of the pulpit sings, very high, and a crack runs down it like a tear.
plays.response: Arguing raises his voice and cracks the glass. Give them a clear chance: he stops and asks, “Do you wish me to go on?” They can de-escalate (an apology, or a question instead of an answer), leave, or keep pushing. If they keep provoking his unstable prison, or attack him, begin Phase 1 (the Glass Sexton encounter).
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 to de-escalate: argument makes him Hostile, and one sincere apology returns him to Indifferent.
plays.consequence: The party knows exactly where the line is.
plays.later: S13: arguing again starts the fight; the listen-patiently route stays open only if they stepped back here.
plays.fallback: If the player won't yield, Maren Talla (if awake) or Yara tugs them out of the chapel before the second crack.
plays.keywords: argue, disagree, debate, shout, contradict, liar, sermon, crack, provoke, sexton

plays.title: A character comes to agree with the sermon
plays.why: The sermon is accurate about the cost of memory; a character who has paid Tolls may find it persuasive.
plays.tells: A player says, quietly, “He's not wrong.”
plays.readAloud: “There is no shame in forgetting,” the Sexton says gently, and for a moment it is the kindest thing anyone has said to you in Corvane.
plays.response: Let it be real. The Sexton is delighted and asks what they would set down if they could. Nothing is taken: he has no Reckoner and no Tithe. The character keeps this belief as long as the player wants; ask whether it changes what they would ring, and note it. The Sexton trusts this character above the others and speaks to them first in S13.
plays.rules: No mechanical effect. Optionally the player rewrites one belief, as with a heartkeep sale; never a loss of control.
plays.consequence: A party member sympathises with the Silence. That is a story, not a problem.
plays.later: S13: he confesses to this character first and offers them the Frost Tongue. S26: this character's view weighs on whether Ysh is sealed, struck or tuned.
plays.fallback: If the rest of the party objects, let the argument happen between players, not with the Sexton.
plays.keywords: agree, sympathise, convinced, persuaded, forget, peace, rest, sermon, believe

plays.title: They lead the silent travelers out
plays.why: Three mute strangers in the pews are an obvious rescue.
plays.tells: A player takes a traveler's hand, or asks who they are.
plays.readAloud: The carter's hand is cold and very heavy, like a child's when it is asleep. He stands when you pull. His sons stand when he does.
plays.response: Hobb and his sons follow anyone who leads them. The walk to Yara's camp is two hours of Extreme Cold and they have no cloaks. Their voices come back within an hour of leaving the chapel. Hobb asks what the man in the glass was, and whether they should go home or wait for the winter to end.
plays.rules: Extreme Cold for the travelers (Commoners): without cloaks, they gain Exhaustion like anyone else.
plays.consequence: Three people are free and owe the party.
plays.later: S15: they help Yara feed the waking Stilled. If Calla rang (S9), they go home to green fields at Kell's Crossing and spread the party's name there.
plays.fallback: If nobody bothers, Yara does it the next morning and charges the party for the cloaks.

plays.title: They listen to the whole confession
plays.why: He has waited 380 years to say it, and patient tables let him.
plays.tells: Players stay seated and ask him what happened on the Quiet Night.
plays.readAloud: “I ordered her to tune them into one long spring. Edda refused, and she wrote it down for me, so that I could never say I did not know. I tuned them anyway. The Key sang against the bells, and the bells cracked on the discord. I have been sorry for four hundred years.”
plays.response: He tells the Quiet Night plainly: the order, Edda's written warning, the Key singing against the bells. He does not say what the Key truly is: 'The Key was never mine to use. I know that now.' At the end he asks someone to lift the crown from his glass head, where the Frost Tongue is set; the glass gives it up to him freely. Then he asks them to end his winter and take him with them, so he can finish his sermon somewhere it can be heard (s13-free-sexton).
plays.rules: No roll for a patient audience. If they read Edda's diary to him (s13-read-diary-to-imber), he weeps and the glass fogs. His age: he has been in the glass since 32 SS, three hundred and eighty years; the Stilled around him have been frozen since 2 SS, four hundred and ten.
plays.consequence: The party holds the Frost Tongue and the confession of the Quiet Night's only living witness.
plays.later: S14: Hieme can be rung. S22: the confession is a source for the truth of the Key, alongside the diary and the Notes. S30: the Glass Sexton finishes his sermon.
plays.fallback: If the table gets restless, he skips to the end: 'Take the crown. I am too tired to wear it.'
plays.keywords: confession, listen, quiet night, imber, sexton, story, frost tongue, crown, edda, patient

plays.title: They ask him about the Key
plays.why: Maudrin's last word mentioned the Key and 'family'; players will ask.
plays.tells: A player says “the Key” or “Maudrin” out loud.
plays.readAloud: He is silent so long you think the winter has taken him. Then: “The Key passed to my daughter, Cassia, when I was disgraced. It stayed in the family's reliquary. Who holds it now? Tell me, and I will tell you what it is.”
plays.response: If they name Maudrin Vesk, he keeps his word: “It is not a tool. It is the Seventh's tongue. It sings the Dreamer to sleep, and I struck the other bells with it to make the calendar behave.” He describes the Vesk reliquary as it was: a vault beneath the family chapel, now under the white palace, with a lock and a weighted tether on the case. He does not know what Maudrin intends. If they refuse to tell him who holds it, he says nothing more about it.
plays.rules: No roll. Session numbers are not information locks (Part 9, Situation 15): let them plan around what they learn.
plays.consequence: The party learns early what the Key is.
plays.later: S22: the truth of the Key becomes confirmation, not revelation. Act IV (Situation 4): his description reveals the tether without a roll and gives advantage on the DC 16 lock if they rob the palace before Maudrin leaves. S24: Maudrin realises they know, and stops bargaining on that point.
plays.fallback: If they don't ask, he asks them, near the end: 'Who has the Key now? Someone must.'
