plays.title: They break the glass and free Imber
plays.why: He asks them to, and a man frozen for 380 years is hard to leave.
plays.tells: A player asks how to free him, or reaches for fire.
plays.readAloud: The glass runs like wax. Inside it there is only an old man in wet ceremonial robes, thin as a rake, shaking so hard his teeth click. “Oh,” he says. “It is cold.”
plays.response: A DC 15 Strength check breaks the glass, or 20 Fire or Lightning damage to it over the scene melts it without harming him (two or three Fire Bolts, one Burning Hands, a Produce Flame held for a minute). As he is freed Imber lifts the crown from his own head and presses the Frost Tongue into their hands. Freed, he is old and frail (Commoner statistics) and does not attack. He needs a warm cloak at once: Extreme Cold applies to him now. He keeps confessing as they walk, and asks to see the Frost Spire before anything else.
plays.rules: Strength DC 15, or 20 Fire or Lightning damage aimed at the glass. Freed Imber uses Commoner stats; Extreme Cold applies. Thunder damage shatters the glass and hurts him.
plays.consequence: The High Sexton of the Quiet Night walks again, and he is a Vesk.
plays.later: S14: if Hieme rings while he lives, he weeps, and the thaw reaches him last. S15: Isolde sees a second Vesk with a claim to the Key, which is the thing the Court fears most (s15-isolde-wants-imber). S22: he is a living witness against Maudrin.
plays.fallback: If the Strength check fails, Yara's saw does it in ten minutes with no roll.
plays.keywords: free, break glass, melt, release, imber, sexton, rescue, fire, strength, thaw

plays.title: They argue on or attack the Sexton
plays.why: Tables that hate the Silence, or think a glass priest is a boss to beat, will push.
plays.tells: A second argument after the first crack, or weapons drawn at the pulpit.
plays.readAloud: The pews crack one after another, like ice on a pond in spring. The Sexton rises inside his pulpit, and the glass of his body is suddenly very sharp. “You came to my church,” he says, “to shout?”
plays.response: Arguing again cracks the glass around him; give them one last chance to stop or leave. If they attack him or keep provoking, run the Glass Sexton from the stat block: frost-form with 95 HP until it shatters, then broken-form with 45 HP. When Phase 2 breaks, the Frost Tongue falls from his crown onto the ice, and the Ringer can grab it before the glass reforms (free if they are adjacent when it falls, otherwise DC 12 Dexterity (Acrobatics) from up to 10 feet). At 0 HP the shell breaks and the frail Imber survives, unless someone deliberately kills him. When it does, play s13-sexton-shell-breaks.
plays.rules: Glass Sexton, two phases. Counterspell does nothing to his Sermon or Icicle Volley: they are not spells. Sermon: DC 15 Wisdom or Charmed until the end of its next turn, Speed 0. Shattering: DC 15 Dexterity when frost-form ends. Calm Emotions can suppress Charmed.
plays.consequence: The fight is joined. Nothing about the Tongue or Imber changes until the shell breaks.
plays.later: S14: they can ring Hieme once the shell breaks. S15: a beaten Imber still confesses, but tells what the Key is only if asked kindly. S22: a witness who was beaten is still a witness.
plays.fallback: If the party is losing, he stops at the end of a round in which nobody struck him and asks, 'Have we finished?'
plays.keywords: fight, attack, sexton, boss, combat, phase, glass, kill, argue, provoke, frost tongue

plays.title: They kill Imber Vesk
plays.why: He caused the Quiet Night; some players want justice, and some want a Vesk out of the way.
plays.tells: A weapon raised over the frail old man after the fight, or at his release.
plays.readAloud: He doesn't raise his hands. He only says, “I know,” and closes his eyes.
plays.response: Ask once: 'You mean to kill him?' He is frail, unarmed and weeping, whether freed or still in the glass (shattering the glass kills him with it). If they do it, he dies and the glass around the chapel goes dull. The Frost Tongue falls from the crown. Say plainly that the only living witness of the Quiet Night is gone.
plays.rules: No roll. Imber has Commoner stats.
plays.consequence: Imber Vesk is dead.
plays.later: S14: Hieme still rings, but no one weeps for the winter. S22: the truth of the Key rests on the diary, the Notes or the Librarian. S24: Maudrin hears of it and thanks them, sincerely, which should feel terrible.
plays.fallback: If the player wavers, he asks only that they finish his sermon for him someday.
plays.keywords: kill imber, execute, murder, revenge, justice, sexton, slay, vesk

plays.title: They use magic to read or free the Sexton
plays.why: Level-5 casters have Detect Thoughts, Zone of Truth and Dispel Magic, and will try them on a man in a block of ice.
plays.tells: A caster asks if he's under a spell, or whether he's lying.
plays.readAloud: Your spell hums in the frozen chapel, and every pane of glass answers it in the same note. The Sexton smiles. “Ah. Tonework. I had almost forgotten the sound.”
plays.response: Detect Thoughts works (he is a living mind in glass): his surface thought is a lullaby and the name Cassia. Zone of Truth is pointless and he says so: 'I have not told a lie since 32 SS; there has been no one to tell it to.' Dispel Magic does not end a winter-moment: it is Hieme's silence, not a spell, and silence-stone has no effect on it either. Fire Bolt, Produce Flame or any fire or lightning frees him gently once the glass has taken 20 damage over the scene; Shatter or Thunderwave breaks the glass and hurts him, and out of the glass he is frail.
plays.rules: Detect Thoughts, Zone of Truth: work, little gained. Dispel Magic: no effect. 20 Fire or Lightning damage to the ice melts it; thunder shatters it and damages him. See s13-free-sexton.
plays.consequence: Magic can free him gently, or kill him by accident.
plays.later: S15: whoever freed him with fire is the one he asks to carry him.
plays.fallback: If a spell fails, he offers the answer anyway; he has nothing to hide any more.

plays.title: They take the Tongue and leave him in the glass
plays.why: Freeing a man who caused the Quiet Night is not obvious, and he is a Vesk.
plays.tells: The party takes the crown and heads for the door.
plays.readAloud: “Then tell me when it rings,” he says to your backs. “I would like to know when the winter ends, even if I am the last to feel it.”
plays.response: He asked to be taken with them. If they refuse, he does not fight; the glass lets the Tongue out of the crown when he asks it to. He asks only that they tell him when the bell rings. When Hieme rings, the thaw reaches him last: he wakes some weeks later, alone, in an empty chapel.
plays.consequence: The Sexton stays frozen for now; the Frost Tongue goes with the party.
plays.later: S15: if they leave him, Isolde finds him before the party does; a Court-held Imber is a Vesk with a claim to the Key, in Maudrin's hands (s15-isolde-takes-imber). S22: he is no witness for them unless they rescue him.
plays.fallback: If they change their minds on the way out, the glass is still warm where they touched it.

plays.title: They climb the Frost Spire
plays.why: The bell is two hundred feet up a tower of ice, and most parties climb.
plays.tells: Players ask about rope, pitons, or how high it is.
plays.readAloud: A spire of ice rises from the centre of the glass forest like a frozen fountain. Inside it the bell hangs motionless, locked in frost. Every breath you take freezes on the air. The bell is singing, so softly you hear it only in your teeth.
plays.response: About 200 feet of ice. Three DC 14 Strength (Athletics) checks get a climber to the top; a failure is a slip: the climber falls 20 feet (2d6 bludgeoning) and starts that check again. A rope team lets one climber Help another (advantage) on each check. If Yara is Friendly she shows the old Sexton's stair on the north face, which removes one check. Exhaustion from the cold applies its -2 per level to every check.
plays.rules: Athletics DC 14, three times. Fall: 20 feet, 2d6 bludgeoning. Help gives advantage. Exhaustion: −2 per level. Extreme Cold saves continue hourly.
plays.consequence: They reach the bell.
plays.later: S15: a sketch of the Spire drawn at the top earns Yara's loyalty (s15-yara-map). S14: anyone who reaches the bell can be the Ringer.
plays.fallback: If the climbers keep slipping, let them find the old Sexton's stair cut into the ice on the north face: slower, one extra hour of cold, no checks.

plays.title: They fly, levitate or Spider Climb up the Spire
plays.why: At level 6, Fly, Spider Climb and Misty Step are on most casters' lists.
plays.tells: A caster asks whether anything stops magic here.
plays.readAloud: Your spell hums, and the Spire hums back, a half-note higher. At its foot, glass heads lift and turn toward the sound.
plays.response: It works. The Spire holds no silence-stones; Hieme is silent, not suppressing. Fly or Spider Climb skips the checks, Misty Step covers 30 feet at a time, and Levitate needs someone pulling a rope. The Glass-Wolves at the base hear the hum and come running, and the Stilled on the ice stairs turn their heads.
plays.rules: Fly, Spider Climb, Levitate and Misty Step as written. Every spell hums; the Spire guards notice.
plays.consequence: A fast ascent, with the guards roused.
plays.later: S15: whoever flew can bring the Tongue down quickly if Isolde arrives.
plays.fallback: If concentration breaks mid-air, the fall rules apply from that height; telegraph the wind before it happens (there is none, which is the point).

plays.title: They fight the Spire's guards
plays.why: Glass-Wolves at the base and Stilled on the stairs stand between them and the bell.
plays.tells: The party approaches the base openly.
plays.readAloud: The wolves at the base of the Spire were lying so still you took them for ice. Then all of them stand up at once.
plays.response: Glass-Wolves guard the base; Stilled watch from the ice stairs and move only when glass breaks or a climber passes within 5 feet. Run the Spire Guards. Each wolf shatters when it drops (shards: 1d6 slashing to creatures within 5 feet), and each shattering cracks the ice stairs a little more. The Stilled stop fighting the moment the bell rings.
plays.rules: A Stilled that hits a climber forces a DC 12 Strength saving throw or the climber slips and falls 20 feet (2d6 bludgeoning). Tell the climber before they pass one.
plays.consequence: The way to the bell is open.
plays.later: S15: Stilled who fought here wake with the thaw and remember; spared or calmed ones count toward the Stilled's trust.

plays.title: They sneak past the guards
plays.why: Parties that avoided the ambush in S11 will try the same here.
plays.tells: Players ask about cover, wind, or a distraction.
plays.readAloud: You pass so close to the nearest wolf that you can see the bubble of air frozen in its eye.
plays.response: A group DC 14 Dexterity (Stealth) check gets the party to the foot of the climb; Yara's map gives advantage and Pass without Trace gives +10. If they were never seen in S11, they also have surprise if it comes to blows. A distraction works too: a thrown glass-flower, a whistle, a Minor Illusion of a running deer draws the pack for two rounds.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 14. Pass without Trace +10. Surprise if undetected in S11.
plays.consequence: They begin the climb unseen.
plays.later: S14: climbing still hums if they use magic; a mundane climb stays quiet.

plays.title: They ring Hieme
plays.why: They carried the Frost Tongue up two hundred feet of ice for this.
plays.tells: A player asks what it will cost.
plays.readAloud: The bell rings once. The sound is high and thin and clear, like a single thread of ice pulled across the sky. The frost on the Spire cracks. The glass trees hum. Everywhere in the forest, something begins to move. The winter is going. Not all at once, but slowly, like a tide turning back.
plays.response: State the Toll and wait for a yes: a Memory, chosen by the Ringer. If they decline, the bell does not ring and no Toll is taken. When it rings, the thaw begins and the Stilled wake over several weeks. If the Sexton is alive, he weeps, wherever he is, and the thaw reaches him last. A Silence spell around the bell only keeps those inside the sphere from hearing it; the ringing still works, because a bell's tone is more than sound (a silence-stone field would stop it, which is why Vaer was chained).
plays.rules: Record the Toll (Toll, Hieme: a Memory). Afterward, decide where the Frost Tongue goes: left in the bell or carried on.
plays.consequence: Hieme is rung. Glassreach begins to thaw.
plays.later: Concord: one more of six. S15: Isolde arrives with Hushmen for the Frost Tongue. S22: the thawed Stilled walk to the Tor if trust is earned. Act IV: the Court's patience ends; its clock moves.
plays.fallback: If the Ringer hesitates, the bell's hum waits with them. A bell that waited four hundred years can wait an hour.

plays.title: They strike Hieme without the Frost Tongue
plays.why: The party left the Sexton's crown behind, or lost the Tongue to Isolde, and tries a hammer.
plays.tells: A player raises a weapon or a mallet to the bell.
plays.readAloud: The Spire groans before you strike it. The frost on the bell thickens, and your breath freezes in the air and falls like hail.
plays.response: Telegraph it first: the bronze rings dead, the Spire groans, and Yara (or Imber) calls out that the bell has no Tongue and striking it will freeze the Spire. If they swing anyway, the frost surges. For the next ten minutes, Extreme Cold saves come every minute at DC 15 (warm gear still means automatic success), and the Glass-Wolves at the base wake. Descending at once ends the effect: every minute spent climbing down is one save, no more. No Toll is asked, because nothing rang.
plays.rules: Accelerated Extreme Cold: DC 15 Constitution save each minute for up to 10 minutes; cloaks and Cold Resistance still succeed automatically. Descent ends it immediately.
plays.consequence: Nothing rings, and the cold bites hard.
plays.later: S13: the Frost Tongue is still in the Sexton's crown (s13-listen-confession), or in Isolde's hands; they need it.
plays.fallback: If a player insists on trying again, the Spire itself cracks a warning down its full length.

plays.readAloud: The Tongue hangs in the bell where it belongs, still faintly singing. Frost is already forming on it again, softer than before.
plays.response: The resonance persists even if the Tongue is later removed, so leaving it is safe for the Concord. It also means Isolde has to climb to take it, which she will not do herself.

plays.consequence: The Frost Tongue stays at the Spire.

Venn's agents in Pellmoor would pay well to exhibit them in Athkatla, and a letter from the Landing says so to their faces; the party can refuse for them.

plays.later: S21: the party knows Maudrin will leave Hallowmere within a day of the second ringing. S23: Isolde stays in Hallowmere 'ill' and sends word of the Strike's route.
plays.fallback: If they won't play along, she takes nothing and reports that they refused.
plays.keywords: isolde, informant, ally, deal, cover story, lost tongue, warning, maudrin, march

plays.title: They head east for Brassfall
plays.why: Thrane's Tongue is with the Ironhorn, and the storms promise allies.
plays.tells: Players ask about the Ironhorn, Kessa, or the storm bell.
plays.readAloud: East, past the last glass trees, the sky flickers over a line of bronze-veined mountains, though there are no clouds at all.
plays.response: Six days around the Ironhorn foothills to Brassfall (Act IV, Branch A). Thrane's Tongue is in Kessa's Tongue-Hall. Tell the players what they know: ringing Thrane brings the storms back, and sailors say it would loosen the Stormwall.
plays.rules: Level 7 after the Glassreach resolution.
plays.consequence: The party takes Branch A first; Vael Tor will be compressed into Sessions 20 and 21.
plays.later: S16A–S19A: Brassfall. S20–S21: Vael Tor, compressed. S22: both bells are needed for the Concord.
plays.fallback: If they can't decide, Yara says Brassfall pays better.
plays.keywords: brassfall, east, ironhorn, thrane, kessa, storm, branch a, road, next

plays.title: They head for Vael Tor
plays.why: Mirel's bell, the Sleepless and the Hush are at the centre of the map, and so is the Key's destination.
plays.tells: Players ask about the Sleeping Hall, Mirel, or the Seventh Bell.
plays.readAloud: South and east, the plain rises to a single hill ringed with grey stones. Even from here, if you close your eyes, you can hear something breathing in its sleep.
plays.response: Vael Tor is about a week from Glassreach by Kell's Crossing (Act IV, Branch B). If they carry Mirel's Tongue (S5), they can ring it as soon as they reach the bell; otherwise the Librarian's courier waits at the Hall.
plays.rules: Level 7 after the Glassreach resolution.
plays.consequence: The party takes Branch B first; Brassfall will be compressed into Sessions 20 and 21.
plays.later: S16B–S19B: Vael Tor. S20–S21: Brassfall, compressed. S22: both bells are needed for the Concord.
plays.fallback: If they can't decide, Imber (if alive) says, 'The Tor. It is where it ends. I would like to see it before.'
plays.keywords: vael tor, sleeping hall, mirel, sleepless, hush, branch b, road, next, tor

plays.tells: The gate check fails, or Aurelie hums a dawn-hymn within earshot of a Hushman.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 on Rook. Aurelie can be broken out with the same methods as Tessa (s06-rescue-tessa) and s09-free-aurelie.
plays.later: S9: s09-free-aurelie frees her. Rook can ask for her release in S6.
plays.fallback: If nobody acts, a Mission acolyte sends a letter for the party's first friend.
plays.title: Cole arrests Aurelie at the gate
plays.why: The smuggling failed, or she sang where she was told not to.
plays.readAloud: Cole turns Aurelie's papers over, then her face. 'No Charter, no writ, no dawn. Take her to the Belfry.'
plays.response: Aurelie is held in Vaer's Belfry as a Charter-breaker, unharmed. The Court offers to trade her for something the party has. Rook hears of it by evening and visits the cell; she will let Aurelie go if the party asks and gives her a reason (Influence DC 15, Rook Friendly to anyone who protects the innocent).
plays.consequence: Aurelie is under arrest. The Court has a bargaining chip.
plays.keywords: aurelie arrested, gate, belfry, charter-breaker, dawn mission

plays.tells: The party asks Brannagh Wick how many boats she can find.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 16 past the cordon. Brannagh's help is automatic if Ila vouches.
plays.later: S22: the ferry-folk keep Court ships on the Mere for a day. S28: who keeps the ledger now depends on who came back.
plays.fallback: If the plan stalls, Sallow insists on being the last off.
plays.title: They evacuate the Old Shore
plays.why: Fighting a Court siege is hard, and ferry-folk have boats.
plays.readAloud: Forty skiffs go out under the grey dawn, the ferry-folk poling across the drowned roofs with their children in the bows. Behind them the Old Shore stands empty and every door is open.
plays.response: Brannagh's pilots take the Old Shore across the Mere in two nights. The Hushmen find an empty village and a notice nailed to the chapel door: 'Search it.' Quill leaves a guard and burns nothing. The ferry-folk will remember who led them.
plays.consequence: The Old Shore is empty and unharmed.
plays.keywords: evacuate, escape, ferry-folk, boats, old shore, siege end

plays.tells: The party barricades the lanes or fights the patrol.
plays.rules: Encounter: Siege patrol (enc-s04-siege-patrol). Influence DC 15 on Quill for the parley.
plays.later: S9: Hushmen watch the Mere road. S22: defended ferry-folk keep Court ships on the Mere for a day.
plays.fallback: If the party loses, Brannagh's pilots take the wounded across the Mere by night.
plays.title: They hold the Old Shore against the siege
plays.why: A protective party will not hand over the village.
plays.readAloud: Quill reads the deadline twice. When he reaches the end the ferry-folk are still standing in the lane, saying nothing, and none of them are afraid.
plays.response: After the siege patrol, Quill accepts a parley: one memory 'for the quota' from a volunteer, and he withdraws for a week. The Court remembers. The Old Shore is changed: windows boarded, the chapel door nailed shut.
plays.consequence: Pellmoor stood, and is changed by it.
plays.keywords: defend, siege, hold the line, old shore, quill parley

plays.tells: The Tongue is with Ila, and a player weighs the pension against the girl.
plays.rules: Deception against Maudrin's Insight (+4) if they lie; the Court's records contradict a lie.
plays.later: S6: Ila is in the dormitory with Tessa (s06-rescue-tessa-with-ila). S23: the favor is called in on the ridge.
plays.fallback: If they won't say, play s04-bargain-refuse.
plays.title: They tell Maudrin where Ila hides the Tongue
plays.why: The party no longer carries the Tongue, and the pension is real.
plays.readAloud: Maudrin does not smile. 'Thank you. That is exactly what I needed, and I will not forget who said it.'
plays.response: Hushmen ride for Pellmoor within a day. Check session-zero Off-limits: Ila is taken Off-screen, never harmed. The Court cart is two days behind, so there is no way to beat it except a courier boat tonight (Brannagh's fast pilot-skiff, 5 gp; play s04-warn-ila). Telling her earns the pension, the exemption and the favor.
plays.consequence: The party owes Maudrin a favor, and Ila is under arrest unless they warn her.
plays.keywords: tell maudrin, betray ila, location, informer

plays.tells: A player asks Brannagh Wick for the fastest boat on the Mere.
plays.rules: No check if the courier leaves tonight; DC 14 Survival to read the Mere in the dark.
plays.later: S6: no Ila in the dormitory. S28: Ila learns who told and who warned.
plays.fallback: If the courier is late, the Hushmen arrive and Ila hides with the households.
plays.title: A pilot-skiff reaches Pellmoor first
plays.why: The party sent word ahead after naming Ila.
plays.readAloud: The skiff slides in under the drowned spire at midnight. Ila is already on the dock with her coat on. 'Brannagh said you'd send,' she says.
plays.response: Ila is hidden at the Pilots' Hall before the Hushmen arrive. They find the Harrow house empty and Quill furious. The Tongue is wherever Ila keeps it.
plays.consequence: Ila is hidden and safe.
plays.keywords: warn ila, courier, skiff, brannagh, hide

plays.tells: The party asks where Ila is, or whether the arrest can be withdrawn.
plays.rules: Influence DC 17 to add anything to the deal (Maudrin's Intelligence). Record in the Bargain Log: one favor owed.
plays.later: S23: the favor is called in, and Maudrin reminds them who it was for. S28: Ila, untithed, grows up to keep the ledger and to ring the ferry-folk's bell.
plays.fallback: If the party argues morality with her, she agrees with every word and keeps the order in her hand.
plays.title: They take Maudrin's offer to release Ila
plays.why: Ila is in the Hall of Tithes and the Chancellor holds the key.
plays.readAloud: 'The girl is well,' Maudrin says. 'She has not been harmed, and she will not be. She can go back to her river. For a favor.'
plays.response: Maudrin offers Ila's release to Pellmoor with the same exemption she would give the party. A Hushman escort takes her to the ferry-stair at dawn. The party owes the favor. If they refuse, the order stands and Ila stays in the Hall of Tithes (rescue alongside Tessa).
plays.consequence: Ila is free in Pellmoor. The party owes Maudrin a favor.
plays.keywords: release ila, exemption, favor, hall of tithes

plays.tells: A player says 'we want it back', or asks Maudrin what the Court plans to do with it.
plays.rules: Influence DC 17 to haggle (Maudrin's Intelligence); Insight DC 15 catches that she is relieved to have it out of the vault.
plays.later: S9: they can ring Ossa after the detour (s09-ring-ossa-later). S23: Maudrin calls the favor and wants every Tongue they carry.
plays.fallback: If they refuse, she says 'Then it stays where it is safe', and means it.
plays.title: They ask Maudrin to give Ossa's Tongue back
plays.why: The Court holds the Tongue and the party needs it for the Concord.
plays.readAloud: Maudrin looks at her glove, then at you. 'Take it. It hums when it is near me, and Quill's reports say it does not hum in the dark. I would rather know where it is.'
plays.response: She returns it for the favor and the silence she asked for. She wants the party to gather the Tongues for her to take at the Strike; she does not say so. Accepting makes her an owed favor. Refusing leaves the Tongue in the Hall of Tithes (s05-take-ossa-from-vault is the theft).
plays.consequence: Ossa's Tongue is with the party. The party owes Maudrin a favor.
plays.keywords: ossa back, return tongue, favor, bargain, court vault

plays.tells: A caster asks whether Cole or the Blank clerk can be charmed, or whether the Hushmen can be slept.
plays.rules: Charm Person: Wisdom save; target knows afterward. Sleep: HP pool; works on Hushmen. Disguise Self: Investigation DC 15 to see through. Every spell hums within 30 feet, so Cole hears the cast.
plays.later: S9: Cole is on the north gate and remembers the caster. Court clock +1 if a spell was used.
plays.fallback: If the spell fails, Cole calls the Gate Hushmen (enc-s04-gate-hushmen).
plays.title: They charm, disguise or put the gate to sleep
plays.why: Level-3 casters have Charm Person, Disguise Self, Sleep and Hold Person, and the gate is a short, dull scene.
plays.readAloud: Your spell hums, and Cole turns toward the sound before he stops turning. 'Interesting,' he says. 'You'll be wanting to explain that.'
plays.response: Charm Person on Cole works (Wisdom save), but he knows he was charmed when it ends and reports it at the Gate Office. Sleep puts the Gate Hushmen down but not the lamplit lanes beyond: someone will find them within the hour. Disguise Self gets past a clerk but not a Reckoner's tuning fork (Investigation DC 15 to see through it). The Blank clerk cannot be charmed: nothing is there to hold.
plays.consequence: The gate is passed, and the Court's record has a flag on the caster.
plays.keywords: charm person, sleep, disguise self, gate, cole, hold person

plays.tells: A player asks where the Dawn Order sits, or whether the Bellwrights have a safe house.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 15 to shake the Hushmen for a day. Influence DC 15 on Rook (Friendly to anyone who protects the innocent).
plays.later: S6: Rook's commission opens early. S23: with no favor owed, Maudrin runs the Strike normally.
plays.fallback: If they wander, Lysse Carrow drops a bone-bound book at their feet.
plays.title: They skip the Assembly and go straight to Rook or the Bellwrights
plays.why: Some tables know the Court is the enemy and want allies first.
plays.readAloud: The Dawn Order's barracks is a long grey building with a yellow door painted over twice. Rook looks up from a map of the Terraces and says, 'You're early. I haven't decided whether I like that.'
plays.response: Rook opens her commission early (S6, Scene 1) and offers a Dawn Order writ for one day. The Bellwrights send Wren Caddock, sewing on a bench outside the Archive, with a friendly question. Maudrin sends a grey rose without a note and two Hushmen follow the party. If the party holds the Tongue, Rook asks what they intend; she will trade a seat at the armory for it.
plays.consequence: No favor to Maudrin is owed. The Court watches.
plays.keywords: rook, bellwrights, skip assembly, barracks, dawn order, wren

plays.tells: A player asks what the sealed shelf behind the Ledger holds, or reads the siege orders ('Ossa relic to the Tithe-Ledger Room').
plays.rules: Alarm: Hushmen in 3 rounds. Sleight of Hand DC 17 for a weight-swap. A Tongue in a silence-stone-lined box doesn't hum.
plays.later: S9: cart searches at the north gate (s09-smuggle-out). S9: ring Ossa after a detour (s09-ring-ossa-later). S23: Maudrin wants every Tongue they carry.
plays.fallback: If they freeze when the alarm sounds, Ansel hisses 'This way. Now.'
plays.title: They take Ossa's Tongue from the vault
plays.why: The Court holds Ossa's Tongue in the Tithe-Ledger Room, and the party needs it back for the Concord.
plays.readAloud: The Tongue lies on a shelf marked SURRENDERED, BELL-WORK. It is cold. When you close your hand on it, it hums once, as if it knew your voice from the Mere.
plays.response: The shelf is weighted like Calla's: lifting it pulls the bell-pull (Hushmen in three rounds). A weight-swap (DC 17 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand)) delays it ten minutes. Four Hushmen search every cart for two days afterward. Ansel will not talk about it.
plays.consequence: Ossa's Tongue is with the party and the Court is hunting it.
plays.keywords: ossa vault, steal tongue, tithe-ledger room, court holds ossa

plays.tells: A player asks about grey aprons, or whether Lysse could walk them in.
plays.rules: Disguise Kit: Charisma (Deception) DC 15 per character; Lysse gives Advantage. Disguise Self, Invisibility and Misty Step are suppressed inside the field.
plays.later: S6: Lysse tells Rook what she saw. S9: Lysse can meet them at the gate.
plays.fallback: If the disguise fails, Ansel comes out of the service passage and takes them to the kitchens.
plays.title: They go in as clerks, or bring Lysse
plays.why: Disguises and a friend on the inside are the oldest vault plan.
plays.readAloud: The clerk's apron is two sizes too big and smells of damp paper. Lysse straightens your collar. 'Walk like you're late,' she says. 'Nobody looks at late people.'
plays.response: Lysse can walk a party into the vault as a clerical squad. Mundane disguises (aprons, a Disguise Kit) work; Disguise Self drops at the threshold because the field suppresses it. Misty Step through a wall is stopped at the edge of the field. Ansel's morning tally still shows the gap. Lysse is old and breathes badly in the cold; she stays at the door.
plays.consequence: The party is inside without a fight, and Lysse knows what they take.
plays.keywords: disguise, clerks, lysse, aprons, misty step, disguise self, invisible

plays.tells: A player corners Ansel in the service passage with a blade.
plays.rules: Ansel is a Commoner-grade clerk. Intimidation does not require death.
plays.later: S6: Wren breaks with the party. S7: Ilam's key still opens the service passage if the party goes back. Act IV: Maudrin's routes must come from somewhere else (Isolde, Edda's Notes).
plays.fallback: If the player wavers, Ansel agrees to everything and walks out.
plays.title: They kill Ansel Quay
plays.why: Ansel is the only man who can sound the alarm, and a threatened party might silence him.
plays.readAloud: Ansel's spectacles fall and he does not pick them up. 'I wanted a cat and a coast,' he says. 'That is all I ever wanted.'
plays.response: Ask once: 'You mean to kill him?' A downed Ansel can be bound; Wren Caddock will find out and take it hard. If he dies, the vault has no keeper, the Hushmen close it for a week, and Wren stops trusting the party. Ansel's Ledger copy and his knowledge of Maudrin's routes (Act IV) are gone. No resurrection.
plays.consequence: Ansel is dead. The Court closes the vault.
plays.keywords: kill ansel, murder, vault steward

plays.tells: A player says 'we read it here' or worries about the Court noticing.
plays.rules: Wisdom (Perception) DC 12 if they do not know the label; a failure costs time only.
plays.later: S13: Imber weeps but the page is not in hand. S22: the Librarian reads the entry aloud for one true memory.
plays.fallback: If they change their minds, the diary is still on the shelf.
plays.title: They read the diary and leave it where it lies
plays.why: Taking it is a theft the Court will feel; reading it costs a few quiet hours.
plays.readAloud: You read by one stub of candle. When you close the cloth, the jar beside it is still humming the note it hummed when you came in.
plays.response: The diary stays on the shelf. The Court never learns. They have the Quiet Night entry and the hint of the Concord in memory only; a Wisdom (Perception) DC 12 search finds it. They cannot read it to Imber in S13 without the diary.
plays.consequence: The Court does not know the diary was read.
plays.keywords: read diary, leave diary, quiet night, edda thorne

plays.tells: The party asks Rook what is on the armory shelves.
plays.rules: No check.
plays.later: S9: ring Ossa with a detour (s09-ring-ossa-later). S23: Maudrin wants every Tongue they carry.
plays.fallback: If the party leaves it, Rook keeps it safe until S9.
plays.title: Rook hands Ossa's Tongue back
plays.why: Maudrin stored Ossa's Tongue in the armory, and Rook now holds it.
plays.readAloud: Rook sets the Tongue on the table between you. 'It hummed all night,' she says. 'I'd rather it hummed in the right hands.'
plays.response: Rook gives it freely and asks nothing. She warns them that Maudrin will want it back and knows exactly where Rook keeps it.
plays.consequence: Ossa's Tongue is with the party.
plays.keywords: ossa tongue, armory, rook, return

plays.tells: A player takes the coup de grace or aims a killing blow at Haldric on the Steps or in the barracks.
plays.rules: Haldric is a Knight (CR 3). His silence-stone shield negates the first spell targeting only him each day.
plays.later: S23: Maudrin's line has no Haldric to break; she arrives colder. S24 and S26: Maudrin carries the grief.
plays.fallback: If the player wavers, Haldric yields his sword and kneels.
plays.title: They kill Haldric
plays.why: The party believes he is guilty and the hearing is going nowhere.
plays.readAloud: Haldric's sword hits the stone. He looks at the palace, not at you. 'She'll hate this,' he says, and does not finish.
plays.response: Ask once: 'You mean to kill him?' He can be knocked out instead. If he dies, the Steps go quiet and Rook steps in front of the party with her arms wide, furious and heartbroken. The Dawn Order splits. Say plainly that Haldric is dead and that a letter in the palace names him 'my son'. No resurrection.
plays.consequence: Haldric is dead. The Strike has two knights and no hesitation.
plays.keywords: kill haldric, murder, execute knight, dead

plays.tells: The party follows Haldric after the hearing, or ambushes his escort in the barracks yard.
plays.rules: Haldric: Intimidation DC 17 only moves him to anger. Influence DC 17 if the party shows him the entry.
plays.later: S23: Haldric remembers who held him. If he is released, Rook demands a public apology.
plays.fallback: If the plan fails, Rook arrives with six knights.
plays.title: They capture Haldric and question him
plays.why: Rook cannot prove the payments; a bound Haldric might talk.
plays.readAloud: He sits very straight on the stable bench, his sword gone, his hands bound in front of him. 'You can't make me say it. And she can't make me stop.'
plays.response: Haldric will not talk about Maudrin. He says 'I serve the dawn' and asks to be killed cleanly. Detect Thoughts is negated by his shield the first time each day; a second casting shows him thinking 'She promised she would come.' Zone of Truth: he declines to answer, which is a tell. Holding a knight is kidnapping in the Dawn Order's law, and Rook will not forgive it.
plays.consequence: The party holds Haldric for a night. The Court knows.
plays.keywords: capture haldric, interrogate, kidnap, question knight

plays.tells: A rogue asks where the armory guards are during the hearing.
plays.rules: Thieves' Tools DC 17. Stealth DC 15 through the yard. If Ossa's Tongue is here too, s09-steal-ossa-too.
plays.later: S9: ring Vaer (s09-ring-vaer). S23: if Haldric holds his office, he rides with Maudrin to get it back.
plays.fallback: If the lock beats them, the young knight forgets to lock the yard gate.
plays.title: They steal Vaer's Tongue while the city watches the duel
plays.why: Every Dawn Order knight is on the Steps, and the armory is a grille and a lock.
plays.readAloud: The barracks yard is empty. Somewhere a long way off a herald is shouting 'Order, order,' and inside the armory a bronze clapper hangs on its peg.
plays.response: The armory grille is DC 17 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) with Thieves' Tools. One young knight stands watch; he is a Rook loyalist and 'misses' the party if they look like they are on her side. The theft is noticed the moment Haldric checks the armory that night.
plays.consequence: The party holds Vaer's Tongue, and Haldric knows.
plays.keywords: steal vaer, armory, duel day, sleight of hand

plays.tells: The party takes Wren to a Hushman, or tells the Court her name.
plays.rules: No check.
plays.later: S18A: Corin Aldeth knows who handed Wren in and is cold. S29: Wren cannot be forgiven because she is Tithed.
plays.fallback: If the party hesitates, Wren steps back before they do.
plays.title: They hand Wren to the Hushmen
plays.why: She sold Tam Harrow's name; some players want justice.
plays.readAloud: Wren does not resist. She holds out her hands. 'I would have done it too,' she says. 'Tessa. Please.'
plays.response: Tessa is moved to a Tithe-house that night and Wren is Tithed within a week. The Bellwrights learn who gave her up. The party loses the Bellwright route and Ansel's loyalty. A rescue is still possible, harder: s06-rescue-tessa-hard.
plays.consequence: Wren is exposed to the Court and Tessa is moved.
plays.keywords: hand over wren, betray, expose, hushmen

plays.tells: The party asks Wren for the layout, and learns Ila is in the next room.
plays.rules: Deception DC 16 or Forgery Kit DC 16; Stealth DC 15. One night: Tithe Clock +1.
plays.later: S9: Wren's Bellwright route carries Tongues past the carts. S28: Ila remembers who came for her.
plays.fallback: If the plan collapses, Ilam Bray opens the service door.
plays.title: They get Tessa and Ila out of the Hall of Tithes
plays.why: Ila was arrested, and the same dormitory holds Tessa.
plays.readAloud: The dormitory door at the end of the corridor is open a hand's breadth. Inside, two girls sit on the same bunk. One of them has an oilskin bundle; it is Ila, and she is humming the response hymn.
plays.response: Same plan as Tessa's, with two children and one closed door: Ila is held, never harmed, and the guards are bored. A forged transfer order covers both. Bet's attic holds both overnight, and Wren's cart takes Ila home. Check Off-limits: both stay behind the party's shield, never described in danger.
plays.consequence: Tessa and Ila are out. Wren is the party's ally.
plays.keywords: rescue ila, rescue tessa, hall of tithes, dormitory

plays.tells: The party asks Ansel where the children went.
plays.rules: Deception or Forgery Kit DC 19; Stealth DC 17. One night: Tithe Clock +1.
plays.later: S29: Wren's fate is the Court's; Tessa is with Bet.
plays.fallback: If the plan fails, Tessa is moved again and the trail goes cold.
plays.title: They break Tessa out of the Tithe-house
plays.why: Wren was handed over and Tessa has been moved.
plays.readAloud: The Tithe-house is a narrow building with grey shutters and a single lit window. A clerk's apron hangs on the line outside.
plays.response: Ansel (if he is alive) knows where Tessa went; Bet Ostrow hears from the clerks. The Tithe-house is lightly guarded by two Hushmen and a Blank. Same options as before, harder: no inside shift-change, no ally on the other side.
plays.consequence: Tessa is out; Wren is gone.
plays.keywords: tessa, tithe-house, rescue, moved

plays.tells: The Influence check fails, or the speaker offers something the Blanks know is empty.
plays.rules: Influence DC 18 to try again after the failure; the second attempt has Advantage if the speaker says sorry.
plays.later: S9: the speaker's description is at the north gate. S22: the Blanks will not march unless a promise is kept.
plays.fallback: If the surge gets dangerous, Ilam Bray drops his gloves and starts helping people off the steps.
plays.title: The speech fails and the crowd surges
plays.why: The Blanks are afraid and a bad promise sounds like a lie.
plays.readAloud: The front rank steps forward. Somebody drops a drawing. A Hushman's glove closes on a shoulder, and the crowd stops being a crowd.
plays.response: The crowd surges, the Hushmen arrest anyone who interferes, and the party must pick a side now: the Blanks (s07-fight-the-line) or the line (leave, or help restrain). Nobody dies in the crush if the party steps in. A Blank at the front asks the speaker's name, forgets it, and asks again, and the surge slows.
plays.consequence: The Blanks do not trust the party yet, and the Court records the speaker.
plays.keywords: crowd fails, surge, failed speech, blanks

plays.tells: A player follows through on the attack.
plays.rules: Ilam is a Hushman (Tough). Child peril: Jonah is not harmed on-screen.
plays.later: S22: the Blanks will not march. S23: Jonah is a hostage on the ridge. S30: Jonah remembers only his mother's face.
plays.fallback: If the player hesitates mid-swing, let Ilam drop his gloves first.
plays.title: They kill Ilam Bray
plays.why: A Hushman walking toward a child looks like a threat to a table that has learned to hate Hushmen.
plays.readAloud: Ilam falls without a sound. The wooden bird rolls from his pocket and stops against Jonah's shoe.
plays.response: Ask once: 'You mean to kill him?' He can be knocked out. If he dies, the crowd screams, Jonah is taken into custody by nightfall, and the Blanks turn on the party. Say plainly that Ilam is dead and that Jonah has lost his father without knowing his name. No resurrection.
plays.consequence: Ilam is dead. Jonah is in custody.
plays.keywords: kill ilam, murder hushman, father, jonah

plays.tells: A player asks Bet or Wren how carts leave the city, or counts the Hushmen at the gate.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 15 at the gate. Each night: Tithe Clock +1.
plays.later: S22: the Blanks march. S28: some Blanks keep the ledger at Pellmoor.
plays.fallback: If the party has no cart, Bet offers hers.
plays.title: They smuggle Blanks out of the city
plays.why: The sweep takes hundreds, and the party has a safe route.
plays.readAloud: Bet's flour cart goes out under the north gate with sacks and six quiet people in the false bed. The Hushmen wave it through because she feeds them.
plays.response: Bet's flour cart, Wren's drains and Ilam's roster can smuggle a few at a time to Pellmoor, the Dawn Mission or Bet's attic. Each night is a Tithe Clock tick. The Blanks remember the promise, and some go to Pellmoor to work the quays with Sela Maunt.
plays.consequence: A handful of Blanks are out of the sweep and the Blanks trust the party.
plays.keywords: smuggle blanks, cart, bet, drains, pellmoor, escape

plays.tells: Ilam deserts and gives the roster; a player holds it up to the line.
plays.rules: Intimidation or Persuasion DC 16 to hold the line's attention; the roster gives Advantage.
plays.later: S9: the Gate Sergeants know the party has the roster (Gate Sweep +2 DC for bluffs). S23: Gaunt is a Court agent against the party.
plays.fallback: If the speech stalls, a Blank reads the next name.
plays.title: They read the Hushmen's roster aloud to the line
plays.why: Ilam's roster names every Hushman, post and shift. A voice that says their names aloud can break a line.
plays.readAloud: 'Sergeant Gaunt,' you say, reading from Ilam's list. 'North gate, third shift. Your sister Orla lives on Cutler's Lane and has not seen you since the Tithe.' The line goes very still.
plays.response: A reading of names to a line of Tithed Hushmen is the cruellest and most effective thing the party can do here. Gaunt withdraws when half her line hesitates. Every Hushman named wonders who else knows. Gaunt will not forgive it.
plays.consequence: The line wavers and the Court's patience thins.
plays.keywords: roster, read names, hushmen, ilam, intimidate

plays.tells: A player asks Lysse who I.V. might be, or carries the letter to the Stacks.
plays.rules: Study, Intelligence (Investigation) DC 16 for Lysse's shortcut in an hour. Never from an absent player's character.
plays.later: S12: they know what to ask him. S13: the Sexton's confession is not a surprise.
plays.fallback: If nobody pays, Isolde's message names him anyway.
plays.title: They ask the Librarian or Lysse who 'I.V.' is
plays.why: The letter is signed with initials, and the Archive knows every name.
plays.readAloud: The Librarian's page turns by itself. 'Imber Vesk,' it writes, in your own hand. 'High Sexton of the Quiet Night. He is not dead. He is waiting.'
plays.response: For one true memory the Librarian names him and says he has been in the glass since 32 SS. Lysse suggests the Archive's Court receipts for the Quiet Night, which are incomplete. The answer is true, and the Librarian adds nothing more.
plays.consequence: The party knows I.V. is Imber Vesk, a Vesk and a Sexton, before they leave.
plays.keywords: who is iv, imber vesk, librarian, lysse, letter

plays.tells: A caster asks whether Edrin is hiding something.
plays.rules: Detect Thoughts: Wisdom save to probe deeper. Suggestion: Wisdom save. Every spell hums within 30 feet.
plays.later: S8: the Court agent reaches Edrin early (Courier Snatch). S10: Edrin will not guide them unless asked kindly.
plays.fallback: If the save succeeds, Edrin still answers because the party has already been kind.
plays.title: They read Edrin with Detect Thoughts or Suggestion
plays.why: A frightened courier with a secret invites mind magic.
plays.readAloud: Your spell hums behind your teeth. Edrin goes pale. 'Don't,' he says. 'Please. I've been paid not to remember.'
plays.response: Detect Thoughts on Edrin shows the name Wyn, the cold of the glass, and a voice in a chapel singing. He is not hiding anything he would not share if asked kindly. Suggestion ('tell us everything') works if he fails his Wisdom save, and he knows afterward. Edrin trusts the party less; the Hushmen hear the spell hum at two streets' distance and the agent arrives sooner.
plays.consequence: They learn the same facts at the cost of Edrin's goodwill.
plays.keywords: detect thoughts, suggestion, edrin moss, interrogate courier

plays.tells: A player asks where Isolde's carriage rests, or whether her seal can be copied.
plays.rules: Stealth DC 15 to reach the case. Forgery Kit DC 16 for the reply. Hold Person and Sleep can disable the driver but the Court notes the hum.
plays.later: S9: Isolde follows with fewer Hushmen (the case is empty), or follows the wrong road. S15: she arrives angry.
plays.fallback: If the plan fails, Isolde invites them to dinner and gives them the orders for free.
plays.title: They waylay Isolde's carriage or forge a reply
plays.why: Isolde carries Maudrin's orders, and a party that wants the Court's plans has a target.
plays.readAloud: The carriage rolls into the yard with grey curtains drawn. The driver is a Hushman. Inside, a small locked case sits beside a pair of silver-rimmed gloves.
plays.response: The case holds the Court's orders to follow the party north: Isolde, two Hushmen, a Sergeant at the waystation. Isolde is not in it. Taking it is a crime against the Court, and the carriage's escort fights to keep it. A forged reply (Forgery Kit DC 16) can send her the wrong way for two days.
plays.consequence: The party knows Isolde's escort and route; the Court knows they were here.
plays.keywords: waylay, carriage, forge reply, orders, isolde, stealth

plays.tells: A player offers a drink and a fee, or notices Edrin's frost-burn.
plays.rules: No check. Perception DC 14 on the road to notice Isolde's carriage.
plays.later: S10: Edrin leaves them at the edge. S12: his warning about the sermon is a free chance to stop arguing.
plays.fallback: If the party refuses, Edrin goes anyway and they can follow his tracks.
plays.title: They hire Edrin as a guide
plays.why: Edrin knows the North Road, wants a reason to return, and will guide for nothing if he is curious.
plays.readAloud: 'The road past the second waystation is not on any map,' Edrin says. 'I'll take you as far as the forest edge. After that the ice does the guiding.'
plays.response: Edrin guides them to Yara's camp; he will not enter the glass. He is a trapper, not a fighter, and he flees if Hushmen appear. He knows the sermon's voice and warns against arguing.
plays.consequence: A guide who knows the road to Glassreach.
plays.keywords: edrin guide, trapper, north road, hire guide

plays.tells: A player looks at the second peg.
plays.rules: Thieves' Tools DC 17 if the grille is not yet open.
plays.later: S9: ring Ossa with a detour (s09-ring-ossa-later).
plays.fallback: If the party leaves it, Rook's loyalist guard hides it for them.
plays.title: They take Ossa's Tongue from the armory as well
plays.why: Maudrin stored it beside Vaer's, and the lock is already open.
plays.readAloud: A second clapper hangs beside Vaer's, grey and cold and water-stained. When you lift it, it hums once, very low.
plays.response: No further roll if the grille is already open. Ossa's Tongue goes into the pack with Vaer's. The Court knows both are gone by the second hour.
plays.consequence: Ossa's Tongue is with the party.
plays.keywords: ossa armory, take both, steal tongue

plays.tells: A player asks Rook whether she can open the armory for one night.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15. Rook is alive (rook).
plays.later: S9: ring Vaer (s09-ring-vaer). If a Silence Warrant follows, Rook is quietly compromised. S22: Rook is an ally.
plays.fallback: If Rook refuses, the armory remains a theft (s09-steal-vaer).
plays.title: Rook lends Vaer's Tongue quietly
plays.why: Rook's case failed, but she wants the dawn rung and the armory is Haldric's.
plays.readAloud: Rook sets the key on the table and does not let go. 'One night,' she says. 'If it goes wrong I never saw you. If it goes right I will be the one standing under it.'
plays.response: Rook cannot give Vaer's Tongue away, but she can 'misplace' the key. She loans it for the night and brings her knights out of the chain-room. Influence DC 15 (Rook starts Friendly to anyone who protects the innocent). If the party apologised after s06-attack-haldric, she softens. Rook will not be the Ringer; she wants to hear it.
plays.consequence: The party holds Vaer's Tongue on loan, and Rook's loyalty is tied to the ringing.
plays.keywords: rook loan, vaer, chain-key, quiet loan

plays.tells: The Ringer is seen on the terraces after dusk, or at the gate.
plays.rules: Encounter: Gate Sweep. Warrant description: +2 to any Court bluff DC about the Ringer. Hide in a crowd: Stealth DC 15 as a group.
plays.later: S9: the north gate is the choke point. S23: the Strike goes for the Ringer first.
plays.fallback: If it turns grim, Rook rides across the terraces with six knights and the Hushmen back away.
plays.title: The Warrant: Hushmen close on the Ringer
plays.why: Vaer rang, and a Silence Warrant means any Hushman may arrest the Ringer on sight.
plays.readAloud: The sun is still on the terraces when the first Hushman steps out of an alley. His gloves are silent. His eyes are on one face.
plays.response: Run it as a pursuit: Gate Hushmen close on the Ringer, grapple, and try to get a hand on the Tongue. The Dawn Order stands aside if Rook won; if she lost, Dawn Order knights join. The party can fight (Gate Sweep, scaled), hide, or leave by Wren's drains. Nobody dies in the street: capture is a cell, not a Tithe.
plays.consequence: The Ringer is hunted in every Court city.
plays.keywords: silence warrant, arrest, ringer, hushmen, pursuit

plays.tells: A player looks for Aurelie in the crowd, or Rook's knight points to a woman singing.
plays.rules: Deception or group Stealth DC 15. Aurelie uses Priest stats (Healing Word, Lesser Restoration).
plays.later: S22: the Dawn Mission is the Stormborn ally (stormborn). S23: Aurelie heals the wounded on the ridge.
plays.fallback: If the party is slow, she walks into the cart herself.
plays.title: Aurelie sings on the terraces and they get her out
plays.why: Vaer rang, and a dawn-priestess is standing under the sun she has waited for.
plays.readAloud: Aurelie stands on the Terrace of Grief with her hood back and her arms open, singing in a voice that carries to the river. 'When the sun comes back,' she says, to nobody, 'I would like to be standing somewhere it can see me.'
plays.response: She is devoted to the party now and she is a liability. The Hushmen will arrest her by dusk. The party can hustle her out through Bet's flour cart, the Dawn Mission's cellar or Rook's barracks (Deception DC 15 or Stealth DC 15 as a group). She tends the wounded on the way.
plays.consequence: Aurelie is free and devoted. She becomes the core of the Stormborn ally.
plays.keywords: aurelie, sing, terraces, vaer, free aurelie, lathander

plays.tells: The party leaves the terraces and Aurelie keeps singing.
plays.rules: No check.
plays.later: S9: s09-free-aurelie. S22: a free Aurelie is the Stormborn ally; if she is never freed, the ally is the Harpers or a crew.
plays.fallback: If the party tries at once, the Belfry door is guarded by two knights who 'forget' the key.
plays.title: The Hushmen arrest Aurelie at dusk
plays.why: Nobody got her out in time.
plays.readAloud: They take her at the last of the light, still singing. She does not resist. The hymn stops in the middle of a line.
plays.response: Aurelie is held in Vaer's Belfry as a Charter-breaker, unharmed. She will be freed by Rook's word, a rescue (s09-free-aurelie), or after a night's pressure from the Dawn Mission. The Court offers to trade her for the Ringer.
plays.consequence: Aurelie is under arrest.
plays.keywords: aurelie arrested, dusk, belfry

plays.tells: The party asks Rook about the cells, or plans a rescue.
plays.rules: Deception DC 15, or Influence DC 15 on Rook. One night in the city: Tithe Clock +1.
plays.later: S22: a free Aurelie is the core of the Stormborn ally. S23: she heals the wounded.
plays.fallback: If the plan collapses, Rook ties the keys to the cell door with a ribbon.
plays.title: They free Aurelie from the Belfry
plays.why: She is in a Belfry cell because of them.
plays.readAloud: The cell is clean and cold. Aurelie sits on the bunk with her hands folded. 'I expected to be afraid,' she says. 'Mostly I'm hungry.'
plays.response: Rook's word opens the door if she won; otherwise a forged release (Deception DC 15) or Wren's drains. Aurelie is unharmed. When freed she is devoted and embarrassed.
plays.consequence: Aurelie is free and devoted. The Dawn Mission is the Stormborn ally.
plays.keywords: free aurelie, rescue, belfry cell, dawn mission

plays.tells: Ilam has been seen on the Terraces asking for a boy with a wooden bird.
plays.rules: No check if Jonah trusts the party. Check Off-limits for child peril; no harm on-screen.
plays.later: S22: Ilam holds the Tor's southern road. S23: Ilam stands between Jonah and the fight. S30: Jonah remembers his mother's face, if she is found.
plays.fallback: If the party misses it, Jonah walks to Ilam himself.
plays.title: Ilam finds the bakery, and Jonah
plays.why: Jonah has asked every hour whether the man with the gloves is coming.
plays.readAloud: Bet opens the door a hand's width and looks past you. 'There's a man here,' she says. 'He took off his gloves on the doorstep. He says he made a bird.'
plays.response: Bring Jonah to the door. Ilam turns the bird over, finds the notch where his knife slipped, and Jonah says, very literally, 'You made that.' Ilam deserts the Hushmen on the spot and gives the party the roster and a key to the service passage. Jonah goes to bed with the bird and the cat.
plays.consequence: Jonah is reunited with Ilam; Ilam is an ally.
plays.keywords: jonah, ilam, reunion, bakery, bird, father

plays.tells: A player asks Ilam, Wren or Bet where the Blanks were taken.
plays.rules: Deception or Forgery Kit DC 16; Stealth DC 15. One night: Tithe Clock +1.
plays.later: S9: reunion at the bakery. S23: a safe Jonah is no hostage.
plays.fallback: If the plan collapses, Ilam opens the service door.
plays.title: They free Jonah from the Hall of Tithes
plays.why: They left him in the sweep, and a rescue like Tessa's still works.
plays.readAloud: The dormitory smells of boiled cabbage. At the end of the corridor, a boy sits on a bunk holding a wooden bird and humming a tune he has forgotten the name of.
plays.response: Same guards, same shift change as Tessa's rescue. A forged transfer order (Deception DC 16) or Ilam's key (if he is an ally) gets the party in. Jonah goes with whoever is kind. Check Off-limits: Jonah is never described in danger.
plays.consequence: Jonah is safe. Ilam may reunite with him (s09-jonah-bakery).
plays.keywords: free jonah, custody, hall of tithes, rescue

plays.tells: A player asks Ilam about the service passage, or asks where Mara Bray's jar is.
plays.rules: No roll for entry with the key. Witnessing another's jar fades it. Hushmen pass every ten minutes (Stealth DC 15 to wait in shadow). One night: Tithe Clock +1.
plays.later: S9: Mara can open her own jar and know Jonah. S28: Mother Sallow opens her wedding-day jar.
plays.fallback: If the key fails, Ansel (if he is alive) unlocks the door.
plays.title: A second visit to the vault with Ilam's key
plays.why: Ilam's service-passage key makes a second visit easy, and there are jars to bring out.
plays.readAloud: The service passage smells of old brick. At the end, the vault door stands ajar and a single lamp burns on the newest shelf.
plays.response: With Ilam's key and the Hushman roster, the party reaches the vault shelves without the front-door alarm. Mara Bray's jar (BRAY, M. 408 SS) can leave in a satchel; only she can open it. Bet's jar, Mother Sallow's and any others the party left behind can go too. Ansel's morning tally finds the gaps.
plays.consequence: The jars are out. The Court knows the vault was entered.
plays.keywords: second vault, mara jar, ilam key, service passage

plays.tells: A note at the first waystation names her escort.
plays.rules: No check. Perception DC 15 to catch her second note.
plays.later: S15: she asks for the Frost Tongue in front of her Hushmen, then offers a private way out (s15-isolde-informant).
plays.fallback: If the party loses her, she finds them at Yara's camp.
plays.title: Isolde follows, as the party's informant
plays.why: The party turned Isolde in S8; she still has to go north.
plays.readAloud: A silver hairpin is pinned to the waystation door. Under it, in her hand: 'Two Hushmen, a coach with a squeaking axle, and my deepest apologies. Be seen to ignore me.'
plays.response: Isolde follows with two Hushmen and leaves notes. She is their informant and a risk: the Hushmen will report what they see. Do not let the party forget that she is not on their side.
plays.consequence: The Court has eyes on the party; the party has a reader inside them.
plays.keywords: isolde follows, informant, hairpin, notes

plays.tells: The party doubles back on the road, or ambushes the carriage.
plays.rules: Isolde: Spy base, Cunning Action. Grappled, Restrained. A captured creature at 0 HP can be knocked out.
plays.later: S15: Tristan Vesk meets the party instead (s15-isolde-wants-imber). S23: a captured Isolde is a bargaining chip.
plays.fallback: If the fight goes long, her Hushmen walk away from the coach.
plays.title: They capture Isolde on the North Road
plays.why: She is alone with two Hushmen and she knows too much.
plays.readAloud: The carriage stops in the dark. Isolde's glass falls and does not break in the mud. 'Oh, you clever people,' she says.
plays.response: Isolde fights one round then tries to Disengage into the trees. If she is grappled or dropped, she is captured. She will talk about her son, the Ironhorn sales and the Court's plan if treated kindly, and spit if not. Her Hushmen surrender when she is down. The Court sends Tristan Vesk in her place.
plays.consequence: Isolde is captured. Tristan Vesk will come north in S15.
plays.keywords: capture isolde, ambush carriage, grapple

plays.tells: A player says 'we have it, let's ring it', or asks the Tidewarden for passage.
plays.rules: Record the Toll (Toll, Ossa). Ringer must be at the bell with the Tongue.
plays.later: Concord: 1 of 6. S15: Isolde's escort may follow them to the Mere. S27: the Choir can sing at the summit if released.
plays.fallback: If the Ringer hesitates, the Cantor waits.
plays.title: They ring Ossa on a Pellmoor detour
plays.why: They recovered Ossa's Tongue in Hallowmere and the bell is a few days away.
plays.readAloud: The Tidewarden waits at the end of the old dock with his oar dripping. He does not ask where you are going.
plays.response: State the Toll and wait for a yes: a memory of someone who has died, chosen by the Ringer. Ila may not be the Ringer. The Tidewarden ferries the Ringer to the belfry and holds an air pocket. If they ring it, the Choir rests and Mother Sallow remembers Davin. If they decline, the bell does not ring and no Toll is taken.
plays.consequence: Ossa is rung. The Choir rests.
plays.keywords: ring ossa, pellmoor detour, tidewarden, toll, belfry

plays.tells: The party asks Yara who sent the letter, or looks for the old woman from Edrin's story.
plays.rules: No check. Wyn is Friendly to anyone who asks about Maren first.
plays.later: S11: Maren is one of the Stilled adults; the gentle route is s11-wake-gently. S15: Wyn leads the waking Stilled to Yara's camp.
plays.fallback: If nobody goes to her, Wyn comes to them.
plays.title: They meet Wyn Talla at Yara's camp
plays.why: The letter led here, and Wyn is waiting by the fire.
plays.readAloud: The old woman by the fire has a trapper's hands and a weaver's patience. 'My family has sat with her four hundred years,' she says. 'We call her the sister. The voice in the chapel is the first thing that ever answered us.'
plays.response: Wyn is Maren Talla's descendant; the Tallas have kept the vigil and the thaw song since the Quiet Night. The voice called itself I.V. and promised Maren would move again. Wyn asks them to wake her gently and is terrified they will use a hammer. She carries the family lullaby and will sing it when the glass warms.
plays.consequence: The party knows who they are freeing and why.
plays.keywords: wyn talla, maren, family, descendant, vigil, sister, camp

plays.tells: A player asks where they can sleep, or how cold the night is.
plays.rules: Extreme Cold: DC 10 Constitution save each hour without gear. Long rest at camp removes one Exhaustion level as normal.
plays.later: S15: the camp becomes a hall for the waking Stilled.
plays.fallback: If nobody asks, Yara charges them for the bed anyway.
plays.title: They rest at Yara's camp
plays.why: Extreme Cold punishes a long rest outside, so tables ask where it is safe.
plays.readAloud: Yara's camp is a ring of lashed tents around a banked fire. The stars here ring faintly, as if the sky were a glass left on a table.
plays.response: A long rest in Yara's tents is safe and warm if the party has cloaks or pays for a place (5 gp each or a keep). Outside, a long rest in Extreme Cold gains no benefit unless the character has warm gear or a fire; ask for a Constitution save at DC 10 and apply Exhaustion on a failure. Yara's whistle keeps the wolves off.
plays.consequence: The party is rested and the camp is a base for S11-S15.
plays.keywords: rest, camp, long rest, tents, sleep, warmth

plays.tells: A player says the name of one of the Stilled, or begins to speak in old Common.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 as an action, Hesk or old Common. Calm Emotions (Charisma save, unwilling only). Tongues: understand and speak any language.
plays.later: S15: calmed Stilled are the first to trust the party. S22: they walk to the Tor only if trust is earned.
plays.fallback: If the party fumbles, Maren Talla (if awake) stands in front of the next one and says its name.
plays.title: They talk the waking Stilled down
plays.why: The Stilled wake terrified and the party has just seen Maren.
plays.readAloud: The man in the glass is shouting at you with his mouth wide open and no sound. When it breaks, he is already speaking: 'The river! The river is cold!' You say his name.
plays.response: A Stilled who hears their name or a calm voice stops, shaking. Influence DC 15 as an action calms one (Indifferent); Calm Emotions calms a group. Tongues lets a caster answer in their dialect. A calmed Stilled stands behind the party and refuses to fight. The ambush ends when enough of them are calm.
plays.consequence: No Stilled is shattered. The party has earned trust.
plays.keywords: calm stilled, talk down, calm emotions, tongues, name, ambush

plays.tells: A player says 'protect the glass' or aims at a wolf.
plays.rules: Encounter: Stilled Ambush, wolves only. Shards: 1d6 slashing to creatures within 5 feet of a shattering wolf.
plays.later: S14: the Spire pack is this pack; if they killed many here, fewer guard the base.
plays.fallback: If the fight goes badly, Yara's whistle draws the wolves off.
plays.title: They fight the Glass-Wolves, not the Stilled
plays.why: The wolves are the real danger; the Stilled are victims.
plays.readAloud: The nearest wolf shatters in a bright spray, and the winter-moment beside it cracks like a plate. A hand moves inside. 'Not that one,' Yara says. 'Not near them.'
plays.response: Each wolf that shatters cracks the nearest winter-moment, so the party must choose between a clean kill and a dangerous crack. Yara's whistle drives the wolves off if the party holds out three rounds. The wolves flee when half of them shatter.
plays.consequence: The wolves are driven off. The Stilled wake in smaller numbers.
plays.keywords: wolves, glass-wolf, fight wolves, protect glass, yara whistle

plays.tells: A caster asks if a Stilled can be understood or whether they are alive.
plays.rules: Detect Thoughts, Tongues, Calm Emotions as written. Dispel Magic: no effect. See any-l3-third-level-spells.
plays.later: S12: they can ask the Sexton better questions. S15: the Stilled trust a caster who spoke their tongue.
plays.fallback: If the spell fails, the Stilled's expression is answer enough.
plays.title: They use magic to speak to, calm or read a Stilled
plays.why: Level-5 casters have Tongues, Calm Emotions, Detect Thoughts and Speak with Dead.
plays.readAloud: Your spell hums, and the glass answers it in the same note. The man inside blinks.
plays.response: Detect Thoughts on a Stilled shows a mind frozen at its last moment: a river, a fire, a name. Tongues lets the caster hear and answer the old dialect. Calm Emotions quiets a waking Stilled. Speak with Dead works only on the dead. Dispel Magic does not end a winter-moment: it is Hieme's silence, not a spell.
plays.consequence: The caster learns what the Stilled saw and feels.
plays.keywords: tongues, calm emotions, detect thoughts, stilled, magic on glass

plays.tells: A caster asks whether the sermon needs to be heard, or a player stuffs wax in their ears.
plays.rules: Silence (spell, 2nd level): 20-foot sphere, no sound, immune to Thunder; no Verbal spells. A deafened creature is immune to the sermon.
plays.later: S13: his trust is lower; the listen route needs an apology (s12-argue).
plays.fallback: If the Silence breaks his patience, he cracks a pew and asks, in a voice that carries through the glass, 'Do you wish me to go on?'
plays.title: They cast Silence or plug their ears
plays.why: The sermon is sound, and the obvious counter is to stop hearing it.
plays.readAloud: The sound goes out of the chapel like a candle snuffed. The Sexton stops mid-sentence and tilts his head. 'Ah,' he says, with no sound at all. 'You are not listening.'
plays.response: Silence (the spell) or deafening works: the sermon needs to be heard, so no save is needed inside. Nobody inside can cast a spell with a Verbal component or speak. The Sexton notices and goes still. He is Hostile unless the party explains; if they drop the Silence and apologise, he returns to Indifferent. A silence-stone field would stop Hieme's winter-moments altogether, but there is none here.
plays.consequence: The party can walk the chapel unaffected but cannot talk. The Sexton is wary.
plays.keywords: silence spell, earplugs, deafened, mute the sermon, plug ears

plays.tells: A player asks what the crown is made of, or whether Mage Hand can reach.
plays.rules: Mage Hand cannot take an object fused into a winter-moment. Strength (Athletics) DC 20 to prise it out cracks the glass and starts the fight.
plays.later: S13: the confession gives it freely (s13-listen-confession).
plays.fallback: If the party backs off, he forgives it with a sigh.
plays.title: They try to take the Tongue from his crown
plays.why: The Tongue is a glittering clapper in a glass crown, and Mage Hand is a cantrip.
plays.readAloud: The invisible hand closes on the Tongue and the crown rings, once, a high thin note. Every pane in the chapel answers.
plays.response: The Tongue is frozen into the winter-moment and part of the crown, so Mage Hand, Telekinesis or a hand-grab cannot pull it free. Forcing it cracks the glass around his head; the Sexton asks, 'Do you wish me to go on?' If they keep going, begin Phase 1. The peaceful ways remain: his confession (S13) or melting him gently.
plays.consequence: The party learns the Tongue cannot be stolen quietly.
plays.keywords: mage hand, telekinesis, steal tongue, crown, grab

plays.tells: Weapons drawn at the pulpit before he finishes speaking.
plays.rules: Encounter: Glass Sexton. Sermon DC 15. Counterspell does nothing to his Sermon or Icicle Volley: they are not spells.
plays.later: S13: a beaten Imber still confesses, but tells what the Key is only if asked kindly.
plays.fallback: If the party is losing, he stops at the end of a round in which nobody struck him and asks, 'Have we finished?'
plays.title: They attack the Sexton on sight
plays.why: A glass priest with a sermon is a boss to a table that wants a fight.
plays.readAloud: The Sexton rises inside his pulpit, and the glass of his body is suddenly very sharp. 'You came to my church,' he says, 'to shout?'
plays.response: Give one last chance to stop: he asks, 'Do you wish me to go on?' If they attack, run the Glass Sexton encounter (enc-s13-glass-sexton) from the stat block: frost-form 95 HP, then broken-form 45 HP. Leaving ends it; he does not pursue. The confession route stays open only if they stop and apologise.
plays.consequence: The fight begins. The shell can break (s13-sexton-shell-breaks).
plays.keywords: attack sexton, fight, glass priest, boss

plays.tells: A player says 'nobody', 'the Church', or names a stranger.
plays.rules: Deception DC 15 (Insight +4). A sincere correction restores the listen route.
plays.later: S13: the confession needs an honest answer to 'who holds the Key?'.
plays.fallback: If the player confesses, he nods and says nothing for a long time.
plays.title: They lie when the Sexton asks who rules the Court
plays.why: A party wary of Vesk blood may not want to tell him it is Maudrin.
plays.readAloud: The Sexton's head tilts. 'Ilse Vesk,' you say, because it is the first name that comes. 'Then it is Ilse,' he says. 'Good. Children of the Court, you are so young. Ilse was my grandniece. She was a very small girl.'
plays.response: Four centuries out of date, he accepts a name he half-knows but notices what does not fit. Deception DC 15 against his Insight (+4); on a failure he says, 'That is not how a Vesk would answer', and trust is spent. He is Indifferent still, but the patient listen no longer works without an honest answer later.
plays.consequence: The Sexton knows he is being lied to, or believes it.
plays.keywords: lie, who rules the court, maudrin, vesk, deceive sexton

plays.tells: A player says 'I'll take them out' while another stays to talk.
plays.rules: Extreme Cold for the travelers (Commoners). Wisdom save DC 15 hourly for those who stay.
plays.later: S15: Hobb's family helps Yara feed the waking Stilled.
plays.fallback: If the split goes wrong, regroup at the chapel door.
plays.title: They split: one lures Hobb out while another stays
plays.why: One character can lead the silent travelers to safety while the others hold the Sexton's attention.
plays.readAloud: The carter's hand is cold and heavy. Behind you, the Sexton's voice goes on, level and kind, like water over stones.
plays.response: Cut between the two groups. The one who leads Hobb's family out faces Extreme Cold for two hours; Yara or Maren (if awake) meets them. The group that stays must keep him talking: an hour of patient listening earns trust. If the sermon takes someone, bring the others back.
plays.consequence: Hobb's family is out, the Sexton is calmer.
plays.keywords: split party, lure hobb, travelers, divide, scout

plays.tells: Broken-form reaches 0 HP.
plays.rules: Imber uses Commoner stats; Extreme Cold applies.
plays.later: S14: they can ring Hieme. S15: Isolde sees a second Vesk (s15-isolde-wants-imber).
plays.fallback: If the party hesitates, Imber holds out the crown himself.
plays.title: The Sexton's shell breaks
plays.why: They fought him and won, or stopped him when it broke.
plays.readAloud: The last of the glass falls away. What stands in the pulpit is an old man in wet robes, thin as a rake, shaking so hard his teeth click. The Frost Tongue lies on the ice.
plays.response: The frail Imber survives unless someone deliberately kills him. He needs a cloak at once and asks, 'Have we finished?' The Ringer takes the Frost Tongue from the ice. He is old, frail (Commoner statistics) and willing to confess if asked kindly.
plays.consequence: The Tongue is with the party. Imber is freed.
plays.keywords: shell breaks, defeated, imber survives, frost tongue falls

plays.tells: A player takes out the diary, or asks if Edda wrote to him.
plays.rules: No roll. Requires the diary (taken in S5 or read at the vault and carried in memory).
plays.later: S14: Hieme can be rung. S22: the diary and his confession agree.
plays.fallback: If they do not have the diary, they read from memory.
plays.title: They read Edda's diary to Imber
plays.why: Edda's words are the last honest account of the Quiet Night, and the Sexton never heard them.
plays.readAloud: You read Edda's entry in a low voice. The glass fogs. When you reach the last line, the Sexton says, quietly, 'She told me. She wrote it down so I could not say I did not know.'
plays.response: He weeps, and the Frost Tongue comes out of the crown into the Ringer's hand without a fight. He asks them to read the last page again, and to take him away from here afterward. The diary shows him what the Key does.
plays.consequence: The party holds the Tongue and Imber's trust.
plays.keywords: read diary, edda thorne, weep, trust

plays.tells: A player offers a cloak, or asks where Imber should go.
plays.rules: Extreme Cold applies. Commoner HP. Constitution save DC 10 hourly without a cloak.
plays.later: S14: he follows to the Spire and weeps when Hieme rings. S15: Isolde sees him (s15-isolde-wants-imber).
plays.fallback: If the party wavers, Yara hands him a cloak and charges the party for it.
plays.title: They take care of the freed Imber
plays.why: A frail man in wet robes in a glass forest is a duty.
plays.readAloud: 'It is cold,' Imber says again, wonderingly, as if the word were new. 'I had forgotten it was a thing a person could feel.'
plays.response: Imber needs a warm cloak, food and a pace he can keep. He wants to see the Frost Spire before anything else, and asks to finish his sermon 'somewhere it can be heard'. Yara allows him in the camp. His age shows: he has been in the glass for three hundred and eighty years.
plays.consequence: Imber is alive and travelling with the party.
plays.keywords: imber, freed sexton, cloak, escort, care

plays.tells: A woken Stilled flinches from a character, or Maren Talla says, 'Some of us remember who held the hammer.'
plays.rules: Influence DC 17; Advantage if Maren Talla or a calmed Stilled vouches.
plays.later: S22: the Stilled walk to the Tor (stilled_trust is Yes). S23: they stand in the Strike as living walls.
plays.fallback: If the check fails, try again after a night of real work; nothing is lost.
plays.title: They win back the Stilled's trust
plays.why: The party hurt Stilled (fire in the clearing, shattered glass) and they remember.
plays.readAloud: A woman steps out of the winter and looks at you. 'You,' she says. 'You woke my husband with fire.'
plays.response: Trust returns slowly and only for real acts: a sincere apology, a memory or Gift given freely to one Stilled, a night guarding the camp. Influence DC 17, with Advantage if a Stilled the party saved speaks for them. Wyn and Maren Talla can vouch. Heroic Inspiration for a Gift given freely.
plays.consequence: The Stilled will walk, but slowly.
plays.keywords: win back, apologise, stilled, trust, amends

plays.tells: A grapple or a drop before her second turn.
plays.rules: Isolde: Spy base. Grappled, Restrained. A creature at 0 HP can be knocked out.
plays.later: S23: a captured Isolde is a bargaining chip against Maudrin (her secrets, her son).
plays.fallback: If she escapes, she reports everything to Maudrin.
plays.title: They capture Isolde at the thaw
plays.why: She came north with a small escort and the party can pin her.
plays.readAloud: Isolde's gloves hit the snow. She does not scream. 'Oh, you wonderful, wonderful people,' she says, and her eyes are on the road.
plays.response: A successful grapple or dropping her before her second turn captures her. Her Hushmen surrender at once. She will talk about her son, the Ironhorn sales and the Court's plans if treated kindly. The Court sends Tristan Vesk next (s15-tristan-envoy).
plays.consequence: Isolde is captured.
plays.keywords: capture isolde, grapple, knocked out

plays.tells: Isolde asks to see the old man in the borrowed cloak, or finds the chapel empty of party.
plays.rules: No check unless the party stops her (Influence DC 15 or a fight).
plays.later: S22: Imber cannot confront Maudrin. S24: Maudrin has nothing to fear from the diary.
plays.fallback: If the party objects, Isolde shrugs and leaves him.
plays.title: Isolde takes Imber back to Hallowmere
plays.why: The party left him frozen, or let her take him.
plays.readAloud: 'For his safety,' Isolde says, taking the Sexton's arm. 'And for the Chancellor's. She will want to meet her ancestor.'
plays.response: Isolde takes Imber under Hushman escort. In Hallowmere, Maudrin silences him in the palace and the party loses a witness. If Imber was frozen, her Hushmen carry him out in his block of ice, melting it with a lamp.
plays.consequence: Imber is in Court hands.
plays.keywords: isolde takes imber, court custody, vesk

plays.tells: Isolde is captured, and a carriage with a Vesk crest arrives.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 on Tristan (Intelligence 13). Isolde's release is a bargaining chip.
plays.later: S23: Tristan is the Court's alternative Chancellor if Maudrin falls. Act V: Tristan offers the party a deal for the Key.
plays.fallback: If the party refuses, he leaves with a promise to return with Hushmen.
plays.title: Tristan Vesk comes north in Isolde's place
plays.why: The party captured Isolde on the road or at the thaw, and the Court sends the next envoy.
plays.readAloud: 'Tristan Vesk,' the young man says, offering a gloved hand. 'The Chancellor's cousin, and, I'm afraid, the one who writes her letters. I'm here about the Frost Tongue.'
